findings.title: Speeds within about 5×10⁻⁹ of c are shown as "1% of light speed" in verdicts and tiles at the All-Star Superman and Superman-benches-Earth presets
findings.location: src/app.html:382 fmtSpeed(): `sig(b * 100, 8).replace(/0+$/, '')`
findings.evidence:
Repro: defaults (comic, concrete, just standing, 2 m). Click the 'All-Star Superman' chip.
- Punch: the verdict reads 'His fist moves at 1% of light speed.' and the tile 'Fist speed: 1% of light speed'.
- Jump: 'Rex leaves at 1% of light speed.'
- Clap: 'Hand speed: 1% of light speed'.
- Stomp: 'Foot speed at impact: 1% of light speed', while the same panel says the lighter-loaded body is at '99.999997% of light speed'.
- Superman-benches-Earth chip, Stomp: 'It also fires him upward at 1% of light speed.' Throw car 45°: 'The car leaves at 1% of light speed'.
The engine gives 1−v/c = 4.4e-11 for the punch, 1.6e-11 for the clap, 3.9e-10 for the jump and 2.6e-11 for the stomp body at Earth. sig() rounds 99.99999999 to the integer '100', and the regex strips its zeros, leaving '1'. Across the 59.5k-state grid this produced 2,829 bogus strings.
findings.expected: About 99.99999999% of light speed, or 'light speed minus x m/s'. Never 1%.
findings.fix: Drop `.replace(/0+$/, '')`. When the rounded value reaches 100, print nines instead. For example: `const s = sig(b*100, 8); if (parseFloat(s.replace(/,/g,'')) >= 100) return '99.' + '9'.repeat(Math.max(1, Math.floor(-Math.log10(1-b)) - 2)) + '% of light speed'; return s + '% of light speed';`

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in the browser and in the engine.

**Browser run** (my script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/c1_browser.js). I loaded dist/preview.html, cleared localStorage so the defaults applied (comic, concrete, 2 m, 180 kg), clicked a preset chip, then read the text of each tab.

All-Star Superman chip:
- Punch: the verdict reads "His fist moves at 1% of light speed. Every punch is a fireball." and the tile reads "Fist speed | 1% of light speed".
- Jump: "Rex leaves at 1% of light speed." and the tile "Takeoff speed | 1% of light speed".
- Stomp: the tile "Foot speed at impact | 1% of light speed", while the same panel says "He gets launched | 99.999997% of light speed".
- Clap: "Hand speed | 1% of light speed".
- Throw (an instance the finding missed): "The car leaves at 99.999997% of light speed … Rex gets shoved backward at 1% of light speed", plus the tile "His recoil | 1% of light speed" and the footing note "he flies backward at 1% of light speed". The same sentence says the car is at 99.999997% and Rex at 1%.

Superman-benches-Earth chip:
- Throw car 45°: "The car leaves at 1% of light speed", plus the status chip and the "Launch speed" tile.
- Stomp: "It also fires him upward at 1% of light speed" and "He gets launched | 1% of light speed".

**Engine values** for 1 − v/c (script: …/audit2/c1_engine.js):

| Value | All-Star Superman | Superman benches Earth |
|---|---|---|
| Punch | 4.40e-11 | |
| Clap | 1.62e-11 | |
| Jump | 3.87e-10 | |
| Stomp foot | 1.06e-10 | |
| Throw recoil | 5.77e-10 | |
| Throw car | | 2.95e-11 |
| Stomp body | | 2.62e-11 |

Every one of these falls in the window 1e-12 < 1−b < 5e-9.

**Mechanism** (app.html:382): `sig(b*100, 8)` rounds 99.99999999 to 6 decimals, giving the number 100. `toLocaleString` prints that as "100", and `.replace(/0+$/, '')` strips its zeros, leaving "1". The regex does nothing useful anywhere else, because `toLocaleString` with `maximumFractionDigits` already drops trailing zeros. Below 1−b = 1e-12 the earlier guard prints "light speed (to the last digit)".

**Reach** (sweep script: …/audit2/c1_band.js; the slider runs from log10 kg 1 to 34). The bug shows over these strength bands (log10 kg):

| Readout | Band |
|---|---|
| Clap | 22.0–23.9 |
| Punch | 22.2–24.1 |
| Stomp foot | 22.4–24.3 |
| Jump | 22.7–24.6 |
| Stomp body | 23.6–25.5 |

The All-Star preset sits at 23.26 and the Earth preset at 24.78, so both fall inside.

**Severity.** Critical is justified. These are the headline verdict sentences on the most extreme named presets, which users will click. The understatement is about 100×, it sits beside correct "99.999997%" text in the same panel, and "1%" is also the page's stated threshold for air plasma, so readers can't tell it is wrong.

**Caveat for the fixer.** One "1% of light speed" string is genuine: "His feet punch into the ground at 1% of light speed" in the jump panel. There `r.push.vB` is about 0.0100c, formatted by `sig(b*100,3)` (b < 0.999), so it should stay as it is.

**The finding's fix works.** I tested it against the cases above: it gives 99.999999% at 5e-9, 99.9999999% at 5.77e-10, 99.99999999% at 4.4e-11, and leaves 99.95% and 99.999997% unchanged.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this. The slider in src/app.html:197 is `<input type="range" id="strength" min="1" max="34">`. At line 430 the value is mapped to a lift of 10^logKg kg, so the right end of the slider is a 10³⁴ kg lift. Line 198, which is also in dist/index.html:198, labels that end '10³⁴ kg (heavier than 10,000 Suns)'.

I loaded dist/preview.html in Playwright Chromium (script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/c2.js). findings.title: Real muscle at the ∞ preset jumps at light speed, while the same panel says real legs cap the jump at about 12 m/s
findings.location: src/engine.js:684 `const p = isFinite(F) ? best.p : Infinity;` (also :689 Eground)
findings.evidence:
Repro: Real muscle, ∞ chip, Jump tab.
- The verdict reads 'Rex leaves at light speed (to the last digit). The ground under him turns to plasma.'
- The tile reads 'Energy into the ground ∞ J'.
- The bullet in the same panel reads 'Real muscle caps his leg speed, so the jump tops out near 12 m/s of takeoff speed however strong he gets.'
At 10³⁴ kg the same settings give 11.7 m/s and 6.86 m. Punch, clap, stomp, sprint and throw all stay capped at ∞ in real mode; only jump bypasses the Hill solver.
findings.expected: About 11.65 m/s and 6.86 m, the same as at 10³⁴ kg. Real-muscle results converge as F→∞.
findings.fix: `const p = (isFinite(F) || ctx.mode === 'real') ? best.p : Infinity;` In Eground, likewise use the computed push.lossB + push.EB in real mode.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in both the engine and the rendered page.

**Engine** (scratchpad/audit2/m1_jump.js, default 2 m / 180 kg body, real mode):
- jump() at F = 1e20 kg·g and at 1e34 kg·g gives v = 11.652 m/s and apex 6.864 m on rigid ground.
- On sand with breakable ground it gives v = 3.35 m/s and Eground = 6.7 kJ.
- At F = Infinity it gives v = 299,792,458 m/s, Ebody = Infinity, and Eground = Infinity whenever the ground fails. This holds on every surface, with the ground holding or not.
- pushApartHill itself is fine at Infinity: it clamps F0 to 1e9·inertialScale and returns finite momenta (push.vA = 12.0 m/s, the same as at 1e34).
- What breaks it is engine.js:684, `const p = isFinite(F) ? best.p : Infinity;`, which throws away that finite result. Line 689 does the same for Eground: `isFinite(F) ? ... : Infinity`.
- The comment there ("momentum bookkeeping is infinity minus infinity") is only true in comic mode. There pushApart returns pA = pB = Infinity, so Math.max(0, pA - pB) is NaN.

**Page** (Playwright on dist/preview.html; localStorage rex-lab-v1 = {inf:true, mode:'real', surface:'concrete', groundHolds:false, action:'jump', H:2, m:180}):
- The verdict reads "Rex leaves at light speed (to the last digit). The ground under him turns to plasma."
- The tiles read "Takeoff speed | light speed (to the last digit)" and "Energy into the ground | ∞ J | ∞".
- A bullet reads "The ground takes ∞ (a magnitude ∞ quake)."
- The same panel also says "Real muscle caps his leg speed, so the jump tops out near 12 m/s of takeoff speed however strong he gets."
- With logKg 34 instead of ∞, the page says "Rex jumps 6.86 m high", with takeoff 11.7 m/s.
- With groundHolds:true the ∞ result is still light speed.

**Correct value.** Under the Hill model the results converge as F0 grows, and the engine's own clamp encodes that. So real mode at ∞ should match 1e34: about 11.65 m/s and 6.86 m at the default size. Real ∞ is a reachable state (the Real muscle toggle plus the ∞ chip). It shows a false light-speed claim that contradicts the page's own bullet, which is major by the rubric. It is not critical because the default mode is comic, where light speed is the intended answer.

**Fix tested** on a scratch copy of the engine (scratchpad/audit2/engine_m1.js) and on a patched preview (preview_m1.html):
- I compared heights 0.3, 2, 50 and 2000 m, all 9 surfaces, ground holding or not, both modes, at strengths 1e2 to 1e34 kg and ∞.
- Only the 72 real-mode ∞ cases changed. Every comic result and every finite-strength result is bit-identical.
- Real ∞ now equals 1e34 exactly at every size and surface.
- The patched page at real/∞/jump shows "Rex jumps 6.86 m high", takeoff 11.7 m/s and finite ground energy, matching 1e34.

The finding's fix, `(isFinite(F) || ctx.mode === 'real')`, gives the same results. The fix below does not need a mode check, and it makes Eground simpler.

**Separate issue, not part of M1.** In real mode on concrete at 1e34 kg (and at ∞ after the fix), the page says "His feet punch into the ground at 0 m/s" and "leaves two craters behind" while the ground takes only about 2.6 kJ ("630 mg TNT"). This looks like a separate wording or engine defect: r.push.vB is the feet's speed at the end of the stroke under the Hill model. It deserves its own check.

findings.title: Real-mode jump says the ground fails and 'two craters' are left, with feet 'at 0 m/s' and 0 J into the ground
findings.location: src/engine.js:688 groundFails = F > RB (compares isometric force); src/app.html:810, :833 (uses end-of-stroke push.vB)
findings.evidence:
Repro 1: Real muscle, Hulk chip, concrete, Jump tab.
- The chip reads 'Ground fails: his feet blast into it'.
- The verdict reads 'Rex jumps 6.75 m high and leaves two craters behind.'
- The bullet reads 'His feet punch into the ground at 0 m/s. That fast, the ground resists mostly through its own inertia…'
- The ground takes 386 J (92 mg TNT); the engine's sink is 1.2 cm.
Repro 2: Real muscle, granite, 10¹² kg. The page shows the same verdict and chip, but 'Energy into the ground 0 J (0 mg TNT)' and '…punch into the ground at 0 m/s… The ground takes 0 mg TNT'. Engine sink is 0. It is the same at the Secret Wars, All-Star and Earth chips and at 10³⁴ kg.
Cause: groundFails compares the isometric force F0 with RB, but under Hill dynamics the force has collapsed before the feet move. The bullet prints the final foot speed, which is 0, not the peak.
findings.expected: On granite: 'Ground holds'. The leg force at speed never exceeds the 153 MN bearing limit, and the sink is 0. On concrete: the feet sink about 1 cm, not two craters, and the bullet should quote the peak foot speed.
findings.fix: In jump(), set `groundFails = !ctx.groundHolds && push.xB > 0` (or Eground > 0). Track the peak vB in pushApartHill and expose it as vBmax, and print that in the bullet. When the sink is under a few cm, say 'dents', not 'craters'.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. I reproduced it in both the engine and the built page.

**Engine.** Script: scratchpad/audit2/m2.js, using the default 2 m / 180 kg body, real mode and groundHolds false.
- **Concrete, Hulk (90,718 kg):** F = 1.246e6 N against RB = 2.25e5 N. groundFails is true, but sink (push.xB) is only 0.0121 m, push.vB is 0, Eground is 386 J and the apex is 6.746 m.
- **Granite, 1e8 to 1e34 kg:** groundFails is true while sink = 0, vB = 0 and Eground = 0.
- **Steel, 1e14 kg and up:** groundFails is true with a 34 µm sink and about 1 J.
- **Comic mode:** fine. There vB is the constant terminal foot speed and the sink is always at least 5 mm when groundFails is true.

**Browser.** Script: scratchpad/audit2/m2_browser.js, opening dist/preview.html with localStorage rex-lab-v1 set to mode real, action jump. dist is newer than src.
- **Concrete at Hulk:** "Rex jumps 6.75 m high and leaves two craters behind." / chip "Ground fails: his feet blast into it" / tile 92 mg TNT / "His feet punch into the ground at 0 m/s. That fast, the ground resists mostly through its own inertia… The ground takes 92 mg TNT."
- **Granite at 1e12 kg, Secret Wars, Earth and 1e34 kg:** the same verdict and chip, with "Energy into the ground 0 mg TNT" and "punch into the ground at 0 m/s… takes 0 mg TNT".

**Cause.**
- engine.js:688 sets `groundFails = !groundHolds && F > RB && !heldBack` from the isometric F0. Under the Hill curve the force has already collapsed once the legs move. I instrumented a copy of pushApartHill (m2e.js): on granite the peak transmitted force is only 0.40–0.49 × RB, so the feet never move.
- app.html:833 prints push.vB, which is the speed at the end of the stroke. Ground drag has stopped the feet by then, so it reads 0. The real peak foot speed is 5.03 m/s on concrete at Hulk and 11.6 m/s at high strength. On sand the line prints 1.73 m/s where the peak is 2.33 m/s.

**A further false claim the finding missed.** In real mode on concrete, the inertial term ρv²A at the peak foot speed is about 5.4 kN at 5 m/s, against 225 kN of bearing strength. Even at 11.6 m/s it is about 29 kN. So "That fast, the ground resists mostly through its own inertia" is false there. It is only true on sand.

**"Craters."** The engine's own result is two dents 1.2–5.1 cm deep holding 0.4–2.6 kJ, roughly one sledgehammer blow, which does not support "two craters".

**Continuum check.** I integrated with a fine step (m2d.js) and with instantaneous activation. At t=0 the force is F0 > RB, so the feet do enter granite, but only 0.03–0.08 mm. That is negligible, so "Ground holds" is the honest label. A percentage of the limit is not, because it depends on the step size.

**Severity: major, not critical.** The default mode is comic, which is correct. Real muscle with the Hulk chip on the default concrete is one click away and contradicts itself on screen.

**Caveat on the suggested fix.** If groundFails is changed alone, the green chip at app.html:818 prints `100*r.F/RB`. That would read "Ground holds (900% of limit)" on granite at 1e8 kg and about 9e6 % at 1e12 kg. The chip must change too.

**Patched copy tested.** I applied the engine fix below to scratchpad/audit2/engine_m2fix.js:
- Real granite now holds at every strength.
- Concrete at Hulk still fails, with a 1.21 cm sink, a 5.03 m/s foot speed and 386 J.
- Comic mode is unchanged.

**Unrelated defect found while testing.** On granite and steel in real mode at about 1e16 kg and above (Earth, 1e34 kg), takeoff speed reaches 14.2 m/s (apex 10.2 m), above vmax = 12 m/s. That contradicts the page's "tops out near 12 m/s however strong he gets". The cause is in pushApartHill:
- F0 is clamped at 1e9 × inertialScale, and inertialScale includes RB, which gives about 1.5e17 N.
- At that size, the 40-step bisection with F taken at the midpoint leaves a force floor of about 1.4e4 N, which is above his body weight.
- The body therefore keeps accelerating. Trace in scratchpad/audit2/m2c.js.
- Fix: leave RB out of inertialScale, or evaluate F at `lo` with 60 or more iterations.

findings.title: Real-mode speeds exceed the caps the page states. The cause is a numerical error in pushApartHill (40-step bisection), not physics.
findings.location: src/engine.js:226 `for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++)` (with the F0 clamp at :208, which includes RA+RB)
findings.evidence:
The page states 'Real muscle caps fist speed near 17 m/s however strong he is', 'jump tops out near 12 m/s', and 'more strength buys force, not speed'. Observed:
- 2 m, granite, claws dug in, 10³⁴ kg or ∞: Punch 'His fist reaches 22.9 m/s' (cap 17). Throw baseball 45°: 139 m/s (whip cap 84.6). Jump on granite: 14.2 m/s and 10.2 m (cap 12).
- Plush 0.4 m, granite, 10³⁴ kg: Jump 8.87 m/s and 3.92 m next to the bullet '…tops out near 2.4 m/s'.
- Plush, granite, claws dug in: punch 15.6 m/s against a cap of 3.4.
Speeds also jump non-monotonically, for example a plush punch going 3.73→15.59 m/s between 10¹² and 10¹⁴ kg.
I patched a scratch copy to 100 bisection iterations. It gives exactly 11.65 m/s for the jump, 17.00 m/s for the punch and 84.60 m/s for the baseball for all of these cases.
findings.expected: At most vmax·s for the move: 17 m/s punch, 12 m/s jump and 84.6 m/s whip at 2 m; 3.4 and 2.4 m/s at 0.4 m.
findings.fix: Bisect S to machine precision: loop until `hi - lo <= 1e-15 * vmax` (or 100 iterations). Optionally drop RA and RB from inertialScale so F0 is not clamped at 1e9×(ground capacity).

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced the finding in both the engine and the built page, and I could not refute it.

**What the page shows.** I set localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' to real mode on granite, opened dist/preview.html and read #bay.innerText:
- **Punch, 2 m, claws dug in, 10^34 kg:** "His fist reaches 22.9 m/s" next to "Real muscle caps fist speed near 17 m/s however strong he is."
- **Jump, 2 m, 10^34 kg:** "Rex jumps 10.2 m high", takeoff 14.2 m/s, next to "...tops out near 12 m/s". It also happens with plain "standing" at 10^20 kg.
- **Throw, baseball at 45°, ∞:** 139 m/s, against a whip cap of 84.6.
- **Plush, 0.4 m, claws dug in:** jump 8.87 m/s and 3.92 m high (should be 2.33 m/s and 0.28 m, about 14× too high), shown next to "tops out near 2.4 m/s". Punch at 10^14 kg is 15.6 m/s against a cap of 3.4.

**More cases from the engine (scratchpad/audit2/m3/repro.js):**
- Punch is non-monotonic for the plush with claws dug in: 3.40 m/s at 10^9, 3.73 at 10^12, 15.59 at 10^14.
- The overshoot also reaches settings close to the defaults: concrete, standing, real mode, at 10^16 kg or more, the baseball goes 86.1 m/s against a cap of 84.6.
- Clap reaches 17.07 m/s at every high strength. test/calibration.js prints "top 17.07 m/s" for punch and clap and still passes them as ok.

**Why it happens.** In the model the relative speed vA+vB can never exceed vmax, because hill(u ≥ 1) = 0. So the correct limits are:
- fist speed at most vmax·s (17 or 3.4 m/s);
- whip speed at most 84.6·s;
- jump speed (mA/m)·vmax·s = 0.971 × 12 = 11.65 m/s.

The bug is in pushApartHill. Its 40-step bisection only resolves S to vmax·2^-40. At that point F0 is still huge: up to 1e9 × (m·vmax²/d + RA + RB), which is about 1.5e17 N for a granite jump. So F0·hill(1 − 2^-41) is still a large leftover force. Every time step adds dv = F·dt/m, so the speed creeps past vmax. Once it is past, s2 > S for every S in [0, vmax], so lo runs up to vmax and the same leftover force is applied again on the next step. My estimate is about 2e-3 m/s per step over roughly 1500 steps, close to the observed +2.5 m/s.

**What I tested (scratch copies of engine.js only; nothing in the project was edited):**
- **100 bisection iterations:** gives exactly 17.0000 (punch), 11.6520 (jump), 84.6000 (whip), 3.4000 / 2.3304 (plush) and 17.000 (clap) in every case, including ∞.
- **Tolerance stop `hi - lo <= 1e-15*vmax`, as the finding suggests:** not good enough. It still overshoots, giving 17.01 and a plush punch of 3.44.
- **Evaluating F at `hi`:** undershoots instead (16.99, 3.36).

With the 100-iteration patch, calibration.js passes (punch and clap tops change from 17.07 to 17.00) and sweep.js passes (5184 contexts, 0 problems). The sweep took 161 s; the timing benchmark showed the real-mode engine about 1.45× slower (82 to 119 ms).

**Severity.** These are wrong numbers in reachable states, and they contradict a cap the page states in the same panel, so this is major rather than critical: it needs real mode, and the large overshoots need granite or claws dug in plus high strength.

**Related defects this fix does not cover.** I found these while reproducing; they are separate findings:

- Bullet: "with no air it would have gone 0.000000000054 mm"

The drag bullet then divides one round-off value by another. At 89° the numbers are sensible: the car flies 1.99 m and the tile reads "footing gives at 7.75 MN". findings.title: Pull is non-relativistic: with bolted footing Rex drags objects 10 m faster than light
findings.location: src/engine.js:812 `t10m: Math.sqrt(2 * 10 / accel)`; verdict src/app.html (bayPull)
findings.evidence:
Repro: Bolted to the planet, All-Star Superman chip, Pull, car. The verdict reads 'Rex drags it 10 m in 0.13 ns.' Light takes 33.4 ns to cover 10 m, so this is an average of about 257 c.
- 10²⁰ kg, plush: '10 m in 5.2 ns'.
- C-17 at 10²⁰ kg, 2 m: '62 ns'. The final speed is 2×10/t = 3.2×10⁸ m/s, which is above c.
- ∞: '10 m in 0 ns'.
The Assumptions card states 'Relativity is built in: … nothing passes light speed.'
findings.expected: t ≥ 33.4 ns. Under constant force f on mass M: x = (Mc²/f)(√(1+(ft/Mc)²) − 1). At ∞ the answer is 'about 33 ns (light-speed limited)'.
findings.fix: Invert the engine's xOfT: `t = (M*c/f) * Math.sqrt(Math.pow(1 + 10*f/(M*c*c), 2) - 1)`. Or at minimum `Math.max(Math.sqrt(20/accel), 10/K.c)`. Use the same in the verdict.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in both the engine and the built page. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/m7/: repro.js (engine), browser.js and b2.js (Playwright on dist/preview.html with localStorage state set), and fix.js (checks the fix).

**Cause.** src/engine.js:812 sets `t10m: net > 0 ? Math.sqrt(2 * 10 / accel) : Infinity`. That is the Newtonian formula, with no light-speed cap. Every other motion in the engine uses relativistic momentum (xOfT, momentumToV, pushApart). bayPull (src/app.html:979) prints the value as 'Rex drags it 10 m in ' + fmtTime(r.t10m).

**What the page shows.** Settings: comic mode, concrete, 2 m / 180 kg, anchor 'bolted', action pull.
- All-Star Superman chip (1.814e23 kg), car: "Rex drags it 10 m in 0.13 ns." Light needs 33.4 ns for 10 m, so this averages about 255 c. Classical final speed is 510 c.
- 1e20 kg, car: "5.6 ns". The plush preset (H 0.3, m 0.5) gives "5.2 ns", as the finding says.
- 1e20 kg, C-17 (id cc177): "62 ns". The implied final speed is 20/t = 3.2e8 m/s, which is faster than light. The correct time is 70.5 ns, arriving at 0.773 c.
- ∞, car: "Rex drags it 10 m in 0 ns."
- 1e34 kg (the slider maximum), car: "0.00000056 ns."

The page's Assumptions card, as rendered, says: "Relativity is built in. Speeds come from momentum, so nothing passes light speed." The pull verdict contradicts it.

**Scope.** Only the 'Bolted to the planet' anchor reaches this. With friction or braced footing, anchorCapacity caps the usable force at a finite friction or shear value, so the acceleration stays small. Under bolted, anchor R is Infinity and usable = F.
- The error passes 1% from about 1e16 kg (engine 557 ns vs correct 558 ns, final speed 0.12 c). At All-Star, the Earth chip, ∞ and the top of the slider it is off by orders of magnitude.

So this is a wrong number plus a false claim, but only in a reachable, non-default state. That makes it major, not critical.

**Correct physics.** Under constant force from rest (hyperbolic motion), x(t) = (c²/a)(√(1+(at/c)²) − 1). Inverting gives an exact, stable closed form: t² = 2x/a + (x/c)². This is the inverse of the engine's own xOfT: plugging the result back in returns exactly 10 m in every case I tested.

**The finding's suggested fix is numerically broken.** `(M*c/f)*Math.sqrt(Math.pow(1 + 10*f/(M*c*c), 2) - 1)` loses almost all precision when x = 10f/(Mc²) is about 1e-16:
- At 511 kg, bolted, car, it gives 2.798 s where the correct value is 2.503 s, a 12% error at the strongest-human setting.
- At ∞ it gives NaN, which fmtTime renders as "∞". The verdict would then say the drag takes forever at infinite strength.

The fallback `Math.max(Math.sqrt(20/accel), 10/K.c)` is not exact either. For the C-17 at 1e20 it still gives 62 ns, which still implies a final speed above c.

**Checks on the corrected formula.** It is identical to the current output at ordinary strengths (0.18487 s at Hulk 100 t, 2.5027 s at 511 kg). It gives 33.4 ns at All-Star, ∞ and 1e34, and 70.5 ns for the C-17 at 1e20.

**Side note (separate issue, not part of M7).** pull() always divides by obj.m + body.m. Under 'bolted' Rex cannot move, so only the load should be accelerated. This is about 6% for the car, but for a light pullable object such as the baseball the acceleration is about 1,240 times too low.

src/engine.js:812, exact relativistic time from rest under constant force. It is stable at any strength and handles F = ∞ (it gives 10/c):

  canMove: net > 0, accel, t10m: net > 0 ? Math.sqrt(2 * 10 / accel + (10 / K.c) ** 2) : Infinity,
  vEnd: net > 0 ? momentumToV(net * Math.sqrt(2 * 10 / accel + (10 / K.c) ** 2), obj.m + body.m) : 0,

(momentumToV(Infinity, m) already returns K.c, so ∞ is safe.)

src/app.html:979, keep the sentence and add an honest note when the load ends up relativistic. This matches the page's own 1%-of-c rule for throws:

With the engine line alone, the verdicts become: All-Star / ∞ / 1e34, car: '33 ns'; 1e20, C-17: '70 ns'. Ordinary strengths are unchanged. Do not use the finding's `Math.pow(1 + x, 2) - 1` form: it gives 2.80 s instead of 2.50 s at 511 kg and NaN, displayed as '∞', at infinite strength.

findings.title: Atlas feat 'Simulate' says Rex can't budge the sky ('needs 1× more strength', 'Strength: 100% of what's needed')

findings.evidence:
Repro: Famous feats → 'Atlas holds up the heavens' → Simulate.
- The verdict reads 'Rex can't budge it. It needs 1× more strength.'
- The chip reads 'Strength: 100% of what's needed'.

findings.expected: 'Rex lifts it…' (strength equals the load).
findings.fix: In runFeat, add a tiny epsilon: `state.logKg = Math.log10(r.liftKg) + 1e-12`. Or make canLift tolerant: `ctx.F >= W * (1 - 1e-9)`.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in the built page. My script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/m10.js. It loads dist/preview.html in Playwright Chromium and clicks Simulate on "Atlas holds up the heavens".

What the page shows:
- Verdict: "Rex can't budge it. It needs 1× more strength."
- Status row: "Strength: 100% of what's needed" and "Below: what would happen if he could"
- Saved state: logKg = 18.707570176097935, obj = 'sky'

Cause: runFeat (src/app.html:1142) stores state.logKg = Math.log10(5.1e18). ctx() (app.html:430) rebuilds F = Math.pow(10, logKg) * g. Math.pow(10, Math.log10(5.1e18)) = 5.099999999999984e18, which is below the sky object's m = 5.1e18. So lift() (engine.js:595, canLift: ctx.F >= W) returns false. The feat sets strength exactly equal to the load, so the correct result is canLift = true.

The page then contradicts itself: it says Rex "can't budge" a load at 100% of the needed strength and asks for "1× more". That is a false claim on a featured, one-click Simulate path, so the severity is major. It is not critical because the default state is not affected.

Scope: I checked every feat with a run config against its object. Only Atlas flips. The Captain America (362.873896) and Hulk (90718.474) values do round down, but no object has those masses, so nothing changes on screen. Captain America and Hulk throw lighter objects. "Superman catches a 777" is meant to fail (247,200 kg against 90,718 kg). The ladder tier clicks (app.html:496 and 1062) use the same round-trip, but the tiers that match an object exactly (bar511, backlift, range150, allstar) all round up, so they pass today. The same latent bug is still there for future data.

The worst round-trip error across all tiers, feats and objects is 3.2e-15 relative, so an offset of 1e-12 in log10 (about 2.3e-12 relative) clears every case. I checked the fix in the browser by preloading logKg = Math.log10(5.1e18) + 1e-12 (script m10fix.js). The page then shows "Rex can lift it, but sinks into the ground doing it." with "Strength: 1× what's needed" and "Ground fails: 220 trillion× its limit". That matches the sky's liftNote, which says the ground already carries this weight as air pressure. The offset does not disturb tier detection (tolerance 0.004 in log) or the calibration check (0.01).
verdict.better_fix:
Fix it at the source so every exact-strength entry point (feat Simulate and ladder tier clicks) rounds up. In src/app.html, add one helper and use it in three places:

  const setKg = (kg) => { state.inf = false; state.logKg = Math.log10(kg) + 1e-12; }; // nudge up so 10^log10(kg) never drops below kg

- app.html:1142 runFeat: `if (r.liftKg === Infinity) state.inf = true; else if (r.liftKg) setKg(r.liftKg);`
- app.html:496: `if (!isFinite(t.liftKg)) state.inf = true; else setKg(t.liftKg);`
- app.html:1062: `set: () => { setKg(t.liftKg); update(); }`

Smallest one-line fix for this finding alone: in runFeat, `state.logKg = Math.log10(r.liftKg) + 1e-12;`.

Alternative fix in the engine, covering all moves: compare with a relative tolerance, `canLift: ctx.F >= W * (1 - 1e-9)` at engine.js:595, and do the same for `canHold` in throwObject. I prefer the app-side nudge because it keeps the engine's comparisons exact.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in both the engine and the built page. I could not refute it.

**Browser repro** (dist/preview.html, cleared localStorage, so default Comic mode; clicked Simulate on the feat cards):
- **Hulk and Thor: Class 100** (90,718 kg, tank, 30°):
  - Verdict: "Rex can hold it, but can't throw it at this angle."
  - Tiles: weight 655 kN, full strength 890 kN, "His throwing push 299 kN · 17% of full strength per hand, 2 hands".
  - Advice: "Try a flatter angle, a lighter object, or more strength."
  - Same feat after switching to Real muscle: "The tank flies 82 cm. Rex gets shoved backward at 1.2 m/s."
- **Sun Wukong's staff** (9,072 kg, 40°):
  - Comic shows the same failure, with a 29.9 kN push against 78.1 kN of weight.
  - Real: "The staff flies 85 cm". The engine gives 2.14 m at 0° in Real.

**Engine check** (scratchpad/audit2/m11.js):
- comicFrac(throwPush) = 0.168 and forceFrac = 0.523.
- In comic mode the tank and the staff fail at 0, 30, 40, 45 and 60°.

**Why the angle claim is always false.** In throwObject, F = sqrt(Fdrive² − (mB·g·cosθ)²) and RB = mB·g·sinθ. So the test F > RB is the same as Fdrive > mB·g, and θ drops out. The "hold but can't throw" result therefore never depends on angle, in either mode. My sweep (scratchpad/audit2/m11sweep.js) ran 220 near-threshold cases (every throwable object, both modes, 0.9–1.1× the threshold strength, angles 0/20/45/70/89°). None changed outcome with angle. So "at this angle" and "Try a flatter angle" are wrong every time this branch is shown.

**Why Comic is weaker than Real.** calibrateComic matches the two modes on a fast shot put (about 14 m/s). At that speed the Hill curve has already cut real force to about a third of its standstill value, and that cut gets frozen into Comic's constant share. For slow, heavy shoves, Real muscle works near its standstill force (52.3% per hand), while Comic stays at 16.8%. As a result Comic needs about 3× more strength than Real to throw any heavy object, for example:

| Object | Real needs | Comic needs |
|---|---|---|
| Car | 1.34 t | 4.0 t |
| Tank | 66.8 t | 198.5 t |
| Staff | 7.97 t | 23.7 t |
| 511 kg bar | 511 kg | 1,543 kg |

The page calls this mode "Comic book" and describes it as keeping a fixed share "at any speed". A reader will take that to mean it drops the speed penalty, not that it is weaker than real muscle. The visible result is that two featured feats fail in the default mode, with a false explanation.

**Severity: major.** The wrong claim is reachable in one click from two feat cards in the default mode. The default page itself (car at 45°) still throws, so most users won't see it, which is why this is major rather than critical.
verdict.better_fix:
1) Text fix in src/app.html bayThrow (lines 718 and 725). This fix is required on its own, because angle never decides the outcome; r.needed is mB·g (load plus arm mass):

```js
out.push(verdict(!r.canHold ? 'Rex can’t throw it. He can’t even hold it up.'
  : 'Rex can hold it, but can’t throw it at any angle: his throwing push (' + fmtSI(r.Fdrive, 'N') + ') is less than its weight (' + fmtSI(r.needed, 'N') + ').'));
...
'Try a lighter object, or about ' + fmtRatio(r.needed / r.Fdrive) + ' more strength.',
```

The "Try a flatter angle" advice should not appear anywhere in this branch.

2) Engine fix in src/engine.js, so Comic is never weaker than Real for throws:
- Rename the current function to `throwOnce`.
- Point `calibrateComic` at `throwOnce`. This keeps the bisection valid; if it called the wrapper, a max() would break it.
- Add a wrapper:

```js
function throwObject(ctx, obj, th) {
  const c = throwOnce(ctx, obj, th);
  if (ctx.mode !== 'comic') return c;
  const r = throwOnce(Object.assign({}, ctx, { mode: 'real' }), obj, th);
  return (r.canMove && !(c.canMove && c.v >= r.v)) ? Object.assign(r, { basis: 'real' }) : c;
}
```

At record-human strength the two modes agree by construction, so the shot put and pitch calibration targets do not move.

3) Update the UI to match the engine change:
- Make `shareText` use forceFrac when `r.basis === 'real'`.
- Add one sentence when that happens: "A slow, heavy shove uses his full standing strength (52% per hand), more than comic mode's fixed 17%."
- With this in place, the Hulk/tank feat shows 82 cm and the staff feat shows 85 cm in Comic mode.

findings.title: Stomp crater up to 10× wider than Earth, shown beside 'Earth blown apart'
findings.location: src/engine.js:714-717 (craterDiameter unbounded); src/app.html stomp crater tile
findings.evidence: Repro: slider to 10³⁴ kg, Stomp. The chip reads 'Earth blown apart'. The tile reads 'Crater: up to 125,938 km wide'. Earth's diameter is 12,742 km. At 10³⁰ kg the crater is 8,413 km wide and the quake is 'magnitude 14'.

findings.fix: In bayStomp, when r.disrupts or crater > ~0.1·R_E, replace the tile with 'n/a: planet-scale' and skip the crater bullet. Optionally cap D in craterDiameter.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. It reproduces in both the engine and the built page.

**Engine check** (scratchpad/audit2/m14.js). Settings: default body, comic mode, concrete, ground not holding. Figures from `stomp().crater`:

| Strength | Crater | Crater / R_E | Quake | Disrupts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10^30 kg | 8,413 km | 1.32 | 13.85 | false |
| 10^31 kg | 16,549 km | 2.6 | 14.5 | false |
| 10^32 kg | 32,551 km | 5.1 | 15.2 | false |
| 10^33 kg | 64,026 km | 10.05 | — | true |
| 10^34 kg | 125,938 km | 19.8 | — | true |

- At 10^34 kg the crater is 9.9 times Earth's 12,742 km diameter, so the finding's "up to 10x" is right. On sand it reaches 146,719 km (11.5x).
- At the ∞ tier the engine returns crater = Infinity and disrupts = true.
- Real (Hill) mode never gets here: the foot is capped near 15 m/s.

**Browser check** (scratchpad/audit2/m14_browser.js). I loaded dist/preview.html with localStorage `rex-lab-v1` = {logKg: N, action: 'stomp', mode: 'comic', surface: 'concrete'}.
- 10^34: chip "Earth blown apart"; tile "Crater | up to 125,938 km wide | impact scaling, upper bound". Bullets: "That is more energy than it takes to blow Earth apart…" and "…it makes an impact crater. The size uses asteroid-impact scaling…".
- 10^30: chip "Quake: magnitude 14"; tile "up to 8,413 km wide".
- So the page says Earth is gone and also gives a crater ten Earths wide.

**Why it is wrong.**
- craterDiameter (engine.js:511-529) is Collins et al. (2005) flat-target, half-space scaling with constant g.
- Above 20 km/s the engine swaps in a stony impactor of the same energy at 20 km/s. At 10^34 kg that impactor is about 1.9e25 kg (L ≈ 2,300 km), far outside the fit.
- No crater on a sphere can be wider than the sphere. Flat-target scaling stops meaning anything well before that: the largest basins known anywhere are about 2,500 to 3,300 km (South Pole–Aitken, Utopia).
- Once E ≥ 2.49e32 J (K.EARTH_BIND), the engine's own flag says the planet is disrupted, so there is no crater to measure.
- Calling it an "upper bound" doesn't make it honest: a bound larger than the planet tells the reader nothing true.
- The previous audit already asked for exactly this guard. Its F5 better_fix, item 3, says to return a planet-disrupted flag when E ≥ the binding energy, and a "global-scale, beyond flat-target crater scaling" flag when D exceeds about 1000–2500 km. Neither was implemented.
- The engine also returns `craterExtrapolated`, but app.html never reads it. The UI never says the crater is an energy-equivalent extrapolation (true for vFoot > 20 km/s).

**Corrections and extensions to the finding.**
1. The bad range starts well below 10^34 kg:
   - Crater > 0.2 R_E (about 1,270 km) from about 10^27 kg on every surface (10^26.7 on ice, 10^27.9 on steel).
   - Crater > Earth's diameter from 10^30.7 kg on concrete, about 2 decades before the disruption flag at 10^32.83.
2. The same unguarded number appears in the throw bay at app.html:778. Moon, 45°, 10^34 kg reads: "crater up to 7,627 km across … felt like a magnitude 14 quake". That is a Moon-mass giant impact, not a crater.
3. At the ∞ tier the tile shows "∞" beside "Earth blown apart", the same contradiction.

**Severity: major.** The preset tiers top out at 6e24 kg (246 km crater, which is fine). The defect shows at the slider's top 7 decades, the "Punch could blow Earth apart" ladder marker and the ∞ tier, all in the default comic mode. It is a reachable state with a physically impossible, self-contradicting number, but not the default view.

findings.title: 'Fireball within a few hundred metres' is wrong for dense or massive thrown objects
findings.location: src/app.html:775 relativistic throw bullet; :727 verdict
findings.evidence:
Repro: Bolted to the planet, 10²⁴ kg, Throw pyramid 45°. It leaves at 13.9% c, with 'It never lands: the air in front of it turns into a fireball… within a few hundred metres of Rex's hand.'
A projectile stops after sweeping roughly its own mass of air, so the path is about m/(ρ₀A):
- pyramid: 173 t/m², about 141 km of sea-level air. That is far more than the whole atmosphere column (10.3 t/m², 14.6 t/m² at 45°), so it exits the atmosphere with most of its energy.
- Empire State Building: 15 km.
- Titanic: 5.4 km.
- Ruyi staff: 4.3 km.
- tank: 1.9 km.
findings.expected: Scale the claim by the path length m/(ρ₀A). If m/A exceeds the column mass along the path, say it punches out through the atmosphere.
findings.fix: Compute `L = o.m / (K.rho0 * o.area)`. Print 'within about ' + fmtDist(L). If o.m/o.area > 10330/sin(θ), use 'tears through the whole atmosphere and leaves Earth, glowing'.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I reproduced it in the browser and checked it against conservation laws.

**What the page shows.** I loaded dist/preview.html in Playwright with localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' set to {logKg:24, anchor:'bolted', action:'throw', obj:'pyramid', angle:45}. The page reads: "The pyramid leaves at 13.9% of light speed. It never lands…". The bullet then says "…its energy, 1.3 × 10¹⁵ t TNT, comes out as a fireball within a few hundred metres of Rex's hand." That bullet is hard-coded at src/app.html:775 and shows for every object above 0.01c. The same sentence appears for:
- the building at 52.8% c
- the ship at 88% c
- a baseball at 99.999992% c (logKg 20)
- every object at Infinite strength

**How reachable it is.** The strength slider goes up to logKg 34. With the default 'friction' footing, these throws turn relativistic at:

| Object | logKg |
|---|---|
| Ruyi staff | 17.5 |
| Tank | 19 |
| Shuttle stack | 20.75 |
| Ship | 22 |
| Building | 23 |
| Pyramid | 24.25 |

With 'bolted' each threshold is about 2 lower. So the whole top third of the slider shows this text for heavy objects.

**Why "a few hundred metres" is wrong for heavy objects.**

1. *Hard lower bound from conservation alone.* At these speeds γ−1 is small. For most of the kinetic energy to become heat, the debris must hand its momentum to an air mass M of at least m: the share turned to heat is M/(m+M). Grant the impossible case where the debris sweeps every bit of air in a sphere around Rex. That sphere still needs radius (3m/4πρ₀)^(1/3), which is 1.1 km for the pyramid. "A few hundred metres" fails even under that assumption.

2. *Upper scale with no breakup.* The swept-mass length m/(ρ₀A), using the engine's own areas:

| Object | m/(ρ₀A) |
|---|---|
| Baseball | 28 m |
| Car | 126 m |
| Tank | 1.9 km |
| Ruyi staff | 4.3 km |
| Shuttle stack | 4.2 km |
| Ship | 5.4 km |
| Carrier | 5.7 km |
| Building | 15 km |
| Pyramid | 141 km |

   These match the finding's numbers. For the pyramid, m/A = 173 t/m², while the air column along a 45° path is ρ₀·Hs/sin45 ≈ 14.6 t/m².

3. *Breakup model* (scratchpad/audit2/m2c.js). The ram pressure ρv² is about 2×10¹⁵ Pa. That drives a shock through the body at roughly 1,000 km/s, after which the debris spreads sideways at 300 to 3,000 km/s. I ran this as a snowplow model through an exponential atmosphere at 45°, measuring how far the object travels before half its energy has turned into heat:

| Object | Distance to release half its energy |
|---|---|
| Car | 0.13 km |
| Tank | 0.4–0.8 km |
| Shuttle stack | 2.6–3.4 km |
| Ship | about 7 km |
| Building | 24–55 km |
| Pyramid | 24 km, or out of the atmosphere still carrying most of its energy |

The fixed phrase came from the previous audit's suggested wording (audit-final.json:769), which was based on a baseball. It holds for baseball- to car-sized objects. It is too short by 10× to 500× for anything heavier than a tank.

**One caveat on the finding's proposed fix.** Its line 'tears through the whole atmosphere and leaves Earth, glowing' is overconfident. With sideways spreading of 3,000 km/s or more, the pyramid can still dump half its energy within about 25 km. The wording should be hedged.

**Severity: minor.** The rubric's 'wrong claim in a reachable state' could argue for major. I kept minor because this is a side bullet in an extreme regime, and the headline numbers (speed, energy) are correct.

**Related problem in the same bullet.** It also says "Air only starts to fuse much closer to light speed". By the previous audit's own figures (audit-final.json:773), the Coulomb barrier is reached at about 0.06–0.08c. So that claim is false at 13.9%, 52.8% and 88% c.
verdict.better_fix:
src/app.html:775 — replace the relativistic bullet with a scaled one. K.rho0 and K.Hs already exist in engine K, and K.rho0·K.Hs = p0/g ≈ 10,330 kg/m².

```js
if (f.relativistic) {
  const sweep = o.m / (K.rho0 * o.area);                                        // path that sweeps up its own mass of sea-level air
  const column = K.rho0 * K.Hs / Math.max(Math.sin(state.angle * Math.PI / 180), 0.03); // air along its path, kg/m²
  const where = o.m / o.area > column
    ? 'along its path up through the atmosphere. It outweighs all the air in its way, so a large part of the energy may leave Earth with it'
    : 'over roughly the first ' + fmtDist(sweep) + ' of its path, about where it has swept up its own mass of air';
  items.push('Past about 1% of light speed the air ahead can’t get out of the way. It is shock-heated into plasma, the ' + o.short + ' vaporizes, and its energy, ' + fmtTNT(r.Eobj) + ', comes out as a fireball ' + where + '.' + (r.v < 0.06 * K.c ? ' (Air only starts to fuse above about 6% of light speed. xkcd’s “Relativistic Baseball” is pitched at 90%.)' : ' At this speed air nuclei also fuse, as in xkcd’s “Relativistic Baseball”.'));
}
```

The scale is an order of magnitude, and breakup makes it shorter.

**Results at 45° with this fix:**

| Object | Text shown |
|---|---|
| Baseball | "first 28 m" |
| Car | "first 126 m" |
| Tank | "first 1.9 km" |
| Ship | "first 5.4 km" |
| Building | "first 15 km" |
| Pyramid | "up through the atmosphere…" |

The fusion parenthetical is now gated by speed. This also fixes the related false claim that air does not fuse at 13.9% c and above.

findings.title: Jump bullet reports the engine's 1%-of-c clamp on foot speed as a physical result
findings.location: src/engine.js:166 `vt = Math.min(0.01 * K.c, …)`; src/app.html:833
findings.evidence: Comic, concrete, from about 3×10¹⁴ kg up to 10³⁴ kg, the bullet always reads 'His feet punch into the ground at 1% of light speed.' At ∞ it reads 'light speed'. The ground-energy figures in the same sentence depend on this cap.
findings.expected: Flag it as a model limit, not a measured speed.
findings.fix: When vB hits the clamp, print 'faster than 1% of light speed (the sim stops tracking ground drag there)'.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in both Node and Chromium (dist/preview.html with localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' set to {action:'jump', mode:'comic', surface:'concrete', groundHolds:false}).

What the page shows:
- logKg 14.3: "His feet punch into the ground at 2,450,000 m/s."
- logKg 14.6, 20 and 34: "His feet punch into the ground at 1% of light speed." The sentence is the same at every one of these strengths.
- ∞: "...at light speed (to the last digit)."

In engine.js:166, `vt = Math.min(0.01*K.c, Math.sqrt(f/c))` engages at logKg 14.1–15.0 depending on the surface (ice is first, steel last). Above that, push.vB stays at exactly 2.998e6 m/s all the way to 10^34 kg.

This is not just a labelling slip. The cap has no basis in the page's own stated physics. The math block says the ground holds the feet with "bearing strength plus an inertial term ρv²A", and it mentions no cap. The Assumptions only disclose a 1%-of-c cutoff for flight. Ram pressure ρv² is the right stopping law in this high-speed penetration regime, and it only needs a γ² correction near c. Without the clamp, the model's own terminal foot speed is sqrt(f/c): 5.5e6 m/s at 10^15 kg, 1.7e7 at 10^16, 1.5e8 at 10^18, and close to c above 10^20.

The clamp also feeds into the headline numbers. Slow feet use up less of the 0.6 m leg stroke, so the body gets more of it. I compared the current engine with the same engine using a relativistic terminal speed instead of the clamp (concrete, comic):

| Lift strength | Takeoff speed now | Without the clamp | Ground energy now | Without the clamp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10^16 kg | 5.3% of c | 2.6% of c | 8.6e15 J | 2.6e16 J |
| 10^17 kg | 1.8e7 % of c → 18.5% of c | 8.3% of c | 3.0e16 J | 2.6e17 J |
| 10^18 kg | 54% of c | 28% of c | 1.0e17 J | 2.5e18 J |
| 10^20 kg and up | about the same | about the same | about 48x too low | (about 1.1 quake magnitudes higher) |

Correction to the 10^17 row: the takeoff speed now is 18.5% of c (5.55e7 m/s); the clamp-free value is 8.3% of c (2.50e7 m/s).

So in a reachable state, the jump verdict "Rex leaves at X% of light speed" is overstated by up to about 2x between 10^15 and 10^19 kg. The "Energy into the ground" tile and the quake magnitude are understated by up to about 48x. The foot speed in the bullet is off by up to about 100x. These states are reached with the default comic mode and the default breakable concrete, on the jump action, across about 20 of the slider's 33 decades. That fits "major" (a wrong number or claim in a reachable state). It is not critical because it is not the default action or strength. Real-muscle mode is not affected by this clamp.

I also found a separate defect that is not part of m3. In real mode, from about 10^5 kg up, the same bullet reads "His feet punch into the ground at 0 m/s. That fast, the ground resists mostly through its own inertia..." This happens because pushApartHill returns the final foot speed, which is 0 after the legs lock, rather than the peak foot speed. It should be filed as its own finding.

On the proposed text fix: it hides the clamp but leaves the takeoff speed and ground energy wrong. Its wording is also inaccurate, because the sim does not "stop tracking ground drag" there; it caps the foot speed.

Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/: m3.js, m3b.js, m3c.js, m3d.js, m3p.js, and alttest/.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Node and in the browser.

1) What the page says. The Sources row "Crater size" reads "Collins, Melosh & Marcus (2005), final = 1.25 × transient". It is in src/data.js:2867 and in the built dist page. In Playwright, on dist/preview.html, the row's textContent matches exactly. The row is generated by build-data.py:246, and data.js carries a "Generated by build-data.py ... Do not edit by hand" header, so the fix belongs in build-data.py.

2) What the engine does. engine.js:526-527 returns 1.25·Dtc only while that is ≤ 3200 m. Above that it uses Collins eq. 27, 1.17·Dtc^1.13/Dc^0.13. The research entry the row is built from (research/final-environment.json, key crater_collins_simple_final_diameter) documents this split itself: "Complex craters (D_tc > 2.56 km): D_fr = 1.17 D_tc^1.13 / D_c^0.13 ... (Eq. 27*)". The table drops it.

3) Reachability. The finding understates it. My scan (scratchpad/audit2/m8/edge2.js) runs comic stomp on concrete at H 2 m, m 180 kg. The complex branch starts at 10^17.954 kg (about 9×10^17 kg), not at 10^20 kg. So every stomp crater on the page above about 2.9 km uses eq. 27. Examples: 10^18 kg gives 3.00 km, 10^20 kg gives 10.13 km (the browser tile shows "up to 10.1 km wide"), 10^25 kg gives 286 km and 10^30 kg gives 8,413 km. Throw craters that size also go through the same function.

4) Size of the gap. eq. 27 divided by 1.25·Dtc is 0.91 at the switch, about 1.0 at Dtc 5 km, 1.09 at 10 km, 1.46 at 100 km and 1.98 at 1,000 km. The headline numbers are computed correctly. Only the description of the method is wrong.

Severity is minor. This is a mislabelled method in a collapsed reference table, not a wrong number. The on-page note (app.html:793) says only "gravity-regime scaling", which is not wrong.

Side observations (not part of m8):
(a) At the switch the crater shrinks as strength rises: comic stomp at 10^17.954 kg drops from 3.199 km to 2.910 km. The published Collins formulas do this too, so it is inherited from the source.
(b) Separate and more serious: the Sources column has no working links. In Playwright, #src-table has 129 rows and 0 <a> elements. Each cell shows raw text such as ",https://impact.ese.ic.ac.uk/static/effects.pdf", with a leading comma, no link and no source title. The cause: el() uses kids.flat(), which flattens only one level. renderModel passes s.sources.map(...) returning [sep, a] pairs, so each pair is stringified. For an anchor element that gives its href. Fix: in el() use kids.flat(Infinity), or in app.html:1167 use (s.sources || []).flatMap((u, i) => [i ? ' · ' : null, el('a', ...)]). - Body mA = 174.8 kg, feet mB = 5.22 kg.
- Push F0·Hill(S/vmax), with vmax 12 and k 0.25.
- Feet resisted by RB + ρA·v² once they move.

| Case | Ground work ∫(RB+ρAv²)v dt | Lower bound RB·xB | Engine | Peak foot speed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hulk, concrete | 2,785 J | 2,747 J | 386 J (7.2× low) | 5.11 m/s |
| logKg 6, concrete | 10,447 J | 9,916 J | 2,086 J | 10.5 m/s |
| logKg 4.5, concrete | 307 J | 306 J | 32 J | not checked |
| Hulk, gravel | 8,615 J | 4,900 J | close | 10.1 m/s (page says 4.98) |
| Hulk, sand | 6,068 J | 914 J | close | 10.7 m/s |

Takeoff speeds match the engine (11.550 m/s for Hulk on concrete), so only the ground bookkeeping and the wording are wrong.

**Causes**
- **Ground energy:** pushApartHill splits the total work by displacement share: lossB = work·xB/(xA+xB) − EB. The feet only move early in the stroke, while the Hill force is near its peak, so this split under-credits them. The result can fall below the hard lower bound RB·xB. A sweep shows the same error on asphalt, concrete and ice (4–10× low) and on steel (1 J against ≥ 2.3 kJ).
- **Ground-failure flag:** jump() sets groundFails = F > RB, using the isometric F0. In real mode the Hill force collapses to RB or below once the body is moving. On granite the feet never move, yet the flag is set at every logKg above about 7.05.
- **"0 m/s":** the bullet prints push.vB, which is the foot speed at the end of the stroke, not the impact speed. On hard ground the feet have already stopped, so it is 0.
- **Inertia sentence:** it is printed unconditionally.

  - On gravel at the quoted 4.98 m/s, ρv² = 50 kPa against q = 161 kPa.

findings.evidence: anchorCapacity derives N(F) = mA g + F sinθ + mB g cos²θ (brute-force check matches R to 8 digits). Once F > R, kinetic friction is μN(F) + dig, which still grows with F, but pushApart keeps applying F − R to Rex. verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Node and in the browser, using my own scripts in scratchpad/audit2/r7/ (repro.js, twod.js, variants.js, cmp.js, browser.js).

**Engine behaviour.** anchorCapacity works out the slip threshold from a load-dependent friction law. The normal load is N(F) = mA·g + F·sinθ + mB·g·cos²θ, and the grip is μ·min(N, Nmax) + dig. throwObject then hands only the scalar anc.R to pushApart (line 630). After slip, pushApart applies F − R to Rex along the push line (lines 146 and 172), so the resistance stays frozen at its value at the slip point. The engine's own statics say otherwise. While N(F) ≤ Nmax, Rex cannot move vertically, and the unbalanced force on him is horizontal: F·cosθ − mB·g·sinθ·cosθ − μ·N(F) = (cosθ − μ·sinθ)(F − R1).

**Default page in the browser** (Hulk tier, car, 45°, concrete, Just standing, comic):
- Headline: "The car flies 10 m. Rex gets shoved backward at 61.5 m/s." (9.29 m/s launch)
- Text: "His footing can only resist 41 kN".
- At the actual push, F = 299 kN and N(F) = 0.977·Nmax = 220 kN. Sliding friction is therefore 0.6 × 220 = 132 kN. Against a horizontal push of 211.5 kN − 6.6 kN, the true unbalanced force is about 73 kN.
- The engine applies 258 kN along the line, 3.5× too much (182 kN of it horizontal, 2.5× too much).

**At logKg 4.5** the engine gives car 6.01 m/s and recoil 29.69 m/s, which matches the finding. The force-corrected 1-D result is 10.48 m/s and 9.99 m/s; the finding's 15.5 m/s recoil is slightly off. My 2-D integration gives a 14.15 m/s car and a 2.84 m/s torso, which also matches the finding.

**Sink check.** At logKg 7 with Just standing, sinkRatio = N(min(F, R))/Nmax = 0.166, and the browser shows no "Ground gives way" chip. Switching to Bolted, with the same push, shows "carrying 100× its limit". The downward load does not depend on whether his feet slide sideways. In fact the engine moves Rex down-and-back along the 45° line into concrete it reports as loaded to only 17% of its limit. That contradicts itself.

**Other settings:**
- Real-muscle mode at the default is also wrong: 4.6 m/s, 3.3 m, 22 m/s recoil, against 10.0 m/s, 11.3 m and 13.7 m/s with the fix.
- At θ = 0 the error vanishes (N does not depend on F), and it is small below about 20°.

**Severity.** I rate this critical rather than major. The default view's headline sentence is wrong by about 3×: with the fix the car flies 28 m and Rex recoils at 21.9 m/s, and an independent 2-D model gives about 24 m/s launch and 16 m/s recoil. The "footing can only resist 41 kN" claim on the same view is false. Every user sees this first.

**Fix tested.** I applied the fix below to a scratch copy. test/calibration.js passes all checks, and test/sweep.js reports 0 problems over 139,240 contexts. The default becomes 16.9 m/s, 28 m and 21.9 m/s recoil. Bolted, θ = 0 and calibration outputs are unchanged.

**Caveats:**
- The reported recoil is still the along-line component.
- The 1-D model still omits the 2-D coupling: holding the car on the line while Rex accelerates adds mB·sinθ·(sinθ + μ·cosθ) to his effective mass. This is why a 2-D run differs further, but that is separate from this defect.
- In the bearing-failed regime the fix follows the engine's stated design ("sinking does not free him along the push line"). For example, baseball at 45° and logKg 8 goes from 16.9 m/s recoil to 0.

I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding is real, and I'd raise it from minor to major.

**How I checked**

- logKg 27: "Crater: up to 1,105 km wide"
- logKg 29: "up to 4,277 km wide"
- logKg 31: "up to 16,548 km wide", next to "Quake: magnitude 15"
- logKg 33: "up to 64,026 km wide", next to the chip "Earth blown apart" and the sentence "That is more energy than it takes to blow Earth apart"
- logKg 34: "up to 125,938 km wide" on the same screen as "Earth blown apart" and "15× the energy to blow Earth apart"
- These match the finding exactly. Sand at logKg 34 gives 146,719 km and granite 120,473 km.

**Thresholds** (my bisection)
- Crater wider than Earth's radius (6,371 km): logKg 29.59
- Wider than Earth's diameter (12,742 km): logKg 30.61
- Wider than half Earth's circumference (πR_E = 20,015 km, the widest a surface feature can be): logKg 31.28
- `r.disrupts` (E ≥ 2.49e32 J): logKg 32.82

**The throw impact line (app.html:778) has the same problem**
- Moon thrown straight up, logKg 29.5: "crater up to 14,533 km across"
- Earth thrown straight up, logKg 31.5: "crater up to 58,062 km across"
- The All-Star object at logKg 30: 19,975 km

**Why the numbers are wrong**
- A crater cannot be wider than πR_E along the surface. Flat-target crater scaling (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005) is calibrated on observed craters up to a few hundred km. The largest basins known anywhere in the solar system are about 2,500–3,300 km (South Pole–Aitken, Utopia).
- Above the binding energy there is no target left to hold a crater, so a crater size is meaningless.
- The page is inconsistent with itself. blastBlock (app.html:632-635) already caps blast radii at πR_E and prints "whole planet", and those rows appear in the same panel as the 125,938 km crater.
- The previous audit's F5 verdict (research/audit-final.json) explicitly recommended this cap: "return Infinity plus a 'planet disrupted' flag … if D_final is more than about 1000–2500 km … flag instead of a number". It was never implemented.

**Severity: major, not minor**
- This is a physically impossible headline number, not a small inaccuracy. It appears in comic mode (the default), on the default surface, across the top ~10% of the strength slider, including the slider's endpoint, where users naturally drag.
- The tile's "impact scaling, upper bound" label implies the number is a meaningful bound, which it is not.
- The "Earth blown apart" chip beside it makes the contradiction obvious, but the displayed value is still false.

**Fix verified**
- I applied the patch below to a scratch copy (preview_fixed.html, checked with ui_fixed.js).
- logKg 8, 20, 27 and 29 are unchanged: 8.79 m, 10.1 km, 1,105 km and 4,277 km.
- logKg 30.5 and 31 now show "planet-scale / crater scaling stops working".
- logKg 33, 34 and ∞ now show "none: Earth breaks up".
- The Moon and Earth throws now read "a planet-scale impact (too big for crater scaling to give a size)".

**Side note, not part of this finding:** throwing 'earth' straight up says "The planet flies 0.0000007 mm" and then reports an impact crater on Earth. Throwing the planet Rex is standing on is a modelling oddity of its own.

findings.title: The air-heating source row claims the table 'matches Anderson's 11 km/s textbook case within ~2%', but the table is at sea-level pressure and shows about 16,400 K, not Anderson's ~11,600 K

findings.evidence: stagnationT(11000) = 16,435 K (the test asserts 16,602 ± 1,500). Anderson's equilibrium-air example (Apollo entry at 11 km/s, about 53 km altitude) gives about 11,600 K. verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute R11 and couldn't. It is real, and minor is the right severity.

**What the page says.** I opened dist/preview.html in Playwright and expanded "Show all 129 sourced numbers". The "Air heating" row reads: "Above: equilibrium-air table computed for this sim (dissociation and ionization included; matches Anderson's 11 km/s textbook case within ~2%; radiation ignored, so an upper bound)". The sentence is built so that the table is what "matches". The text comes from build-data.py:247 and appears in src/data.js:2879.

**What the engine computes.**
- stagnationT(11000) = 16,435 K, which is 16,162 °C. The table is interpolated between 10 km/s (14,060 K) and 15 km/s (27,313 K).
- Stagnation pressure here is ρ0·v² ≈ 1,463 atm.
- In the UI, with punch, comic mode and logKg 8.77, the fist reaches 11,000 m/s and the tile reads "Air at the knuckles 16,228 °C, equilibrium air".

**Anderson's case.** The Apollo shock layer at about 11 km/s (36,000 ft/s) and 53 km altitude is about 11,600 K, against about 58,000 K for a perfect gas.

**My own solve.** I ran the earlier Gibbs equilibrium-air solver (audit/f7refute/eqair.py) through a new driver, audit2/r11/r11.py, using US Standard Atmosphere density at 53 km (ρ ≈ 7.2e-4 kg/m³, so p_stag ≈ 0.86 atm):

| Case | Equilibrium T |
|---|---|
| 10.97 km/s, Anderson conditions | 11,659 K |
| 11.0 km/s, Anderson conditions | 11,691 K |
| 11 km/s, sea-level pressure (1,463 atm) | 16,602 K |

So the solver matches Anderson to under 1%, which is within the "~2%" claimed. The published table at 11 km/s is about 41% above Anderson's figure, because high pressure suppresses dissociation.

**Why it misleads.** The table and its numbers are fine for the sea-level case the sim models. The problem is the validation claim: it is attached to the wrong object. A reader who checks Anderson finds 11,600 K, while the sim shows about 16,400 K at 11 km/s. Anderson is also not among the row's cited sources, so the reader cannot see what case was compared. The engine.js:286-289 comment has the same wording. It does say "at sea-level stagnation pressure", but it still says "it matches".

**Severity.** Minor. The row sits in a collapsed table, the displayed temperatures are correct for the sea-level case the sim models, and only the validation wording misleads.

**Separate bug found while reproducing (not part of R11, likely major).** Every Sources cell in the table renders as plain text such as ",https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/BGH/stagtmp.html · ,https://…". There are 0 `<a>` elements in #src-table.
- Cause: renderModel (app.html:1167) passes a nested array, `(s.sources||[]).map((u,i)=>[sep, el('a',…)])`.
- el() (app.html:299) only does `kids.flat()`, one level deep. Each [sep, anchor] pair is therefore stringified with String(), and an anchor's toString() returns its href.
- Fix: in el(), change `kids.flat()` to `kids.flat(Infinity)`, or use `.flatMap(...)` in renderModel.

findings.title: Crater size jumps at the 20 km/s equivalent-impactor switch (density changes to 3000 kg/m³) and drops 9% at the complex-crater transition
findings.location: src/engine.js craterDiameter() lines 518-527
findings.evidence: At impact speeds of 19,999.9 vs 20,000.1 m/s: ρi = 115 (car) D jumps +27%; ρi = 1000 (stomp foot) +8%; ρi = 8000 (shot) −7%, so the crater shrinks as strength rises. Complex branch: D_tc 2,559 m gives 3,199 m and 2,561 m gives 2,911 m. In the comic concrete stomp, 3,100 m at 10^17.9 kg becomes 3,000 m at 10^18.0. The complex drop is inherited from Collins et al. eqs. 22/27. The density switch is new code.
findings.expected: Crater diameter continuous and non-decreasing in strength.
findings.fix: Keep the impactor's own density in the mapping (m_eq = 2E/v_eq², L = cbrt(6 m_eq/(π ρi))), which is continuous at 20 km/s. Optionally take max(1.25·D_tc, complex) between D_tc 2,560 and 2,785 m so the transition does not step down.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in the engine and in the rendered page. The defect is real, but part of the finding's evidence is overstated.

**Unit level, engine.js craterDiameter() lines 518-527.** Same-mass sphere into a target of 2400 kg/m³, at 19,999.9 vs 20,000.1 m/s:
- ρi = 115: 51.70 m becomes 65.67 m (+27.0%).
- ρi = 1000: 60.59 m becomes 65.67 m (+8.4%).
- ρi = 8000: 70.57 m becomes 65.67 m (-6.9%).
- ρi = 3000: no jump.

The cause is that the mapping above 20 km/s replaces the impactor's density with 3000 kg/m³. At fixed energy and speed, Collins eq. 21 gives D ∝ ρi^(1/3 - 0.26) = ρi^0.073, and (3000/ρi)^0.073 matches the jumps exactly.

The complex-crater branch also steps down. D_tc 2,559 m gives D = 3,199 m, and D_tc 2,561 m gives 2,911 m. Analytically, at D_tc = Dc/1.25, eq. 27 gives 1.17·(Dc/1.25)^1.13 / Dc^0.13 = 0.909·Dc, a 9% drop. That drop is in the published Collins et al. (2005) model itself, not something this code introduced.

**What is not reachable: the car (+27%) and shot (-7%) examples.** I swept throwObject() over every object, at angles 0-90° and strengths 10^2-10^34 kg. The fastest landed impact was 9.49 km/s (Everest). A projectile that comes back down cannot land faster than escape speed, about 11.2 km/s, so the throw path never enters the branch above 20 km/s. The claim that the crater "shrinks as strength rises" because of the density switch is therefore unreachable in the app.

**What is reachable: the stomp foot, with ρi = 1000.** This is comic mode only; in real mode the foot never reaches the 2 km/s crater threshold. On all 9 surfaces, the foot crosses 20 km/s between 10^9.49 and 10^9.50 kg. In that one 0.01 slider step the crater jumps +9.0%, where a normal step adds about 0.6%.

Rendered page (preview.html, comic, concrete, stomp; localStorage logKg set to each value):
- 9.49: "up to 18.7 m wide"
- 9.50: "up to 20.4 m wide"
- 17.95: "up to 3.19 km wide"
- 17.96: "up to 2.92 km wide"
- 18.00: "up to 3 km wide"

So at 10^17.95-17.96 kg the crater does shrink as strength rises. That comes from the inherited eq. 27 step, which my sweep shows at 10^17.4-18.6 kg depending on the surface. Throws of large objects with crater-sized results (pyramid, Everest, range150, Moon) can also cross it.

**Severity: minor.** The changes are 9% or less. They are well inside the model's stated "upper bound / overstates by a few times" caveat, and they show only when scrubbing past two specific strengths. Still, a crater that gets smaller as Rex gets stronger is a visible inconsistency for a critic. The density switch is new code with no physical justification, because the impactor's own density works equally well and is continuous.

**Fix verified on a scratch copy** (scratchpad/audit2/engine_r14.js, check script r14_fixcheck.js). With both changes, comic stomp on all 9 surfaces from 10^1 to 10^34 kg in 0.01 steps has 0 non-monotone or more-than-3% steps (concrete 9.49 → 9.50: 18.7 → 18.8 m), and test/calibration.js still passes all checks.

One side effect: stomp craters above 20 km/s become about 7.7% smaller, a factor of (1000/3000)^0.073. For example, concrete at 10^20 kg gives 9.25 km.

A related labelling nit, separate from this finding: the Sources table entry "Crater size" says only "final = 1.25 × transient". It mentions neither the complex-crater branch (eq. 27) nor the energy-equivalent mapping above 20 km/s.

  - Apex 1.07 million km (Titanic, 30°, Bolted, 17.18; the page says 45.9 days): it returns after 91–261 days.
  - So the two-body result is badly wrong from about 0.7 of the Hill radius outward, and simply wrong beyond it.

**3. Vacuum ghost has no time limit: confirmed**
- fly({v0: 11186, thetaDeg: 89, Cd: 0}) returns landed after 474.5 years with an apex of 2.63e8 km. The vacuum branch never checks tMax.
- Users can see this. Shot, 45°, default friction anchor, 8.45: "Air is the real limit on range: with no air it would have gone 19,964 km". That ghost's apex is 1.58 million km, so it would have left Earth.

**Refuted part: the pyramid example**
- Pyramid, 45°, Bolted, 16.91 reproduces exactly: "flies 19,832 km", "top 445,524 km · 12.5 days". The next slider step (16.92) escapes, so the pyramid never shows a past-Hill arc at slider resolution.
- At 445,000 km the Sun's tide changes the flight time by under 4% in my three-body check (12.2–12.6 days against 12.6 days). The Moon matters only if it happens to be nearby.
- So passing the Moon's distance is not a wrong number in itself. It is a disclosure gap. The math line "Above 150 km the arc is solved exactly (Kepler)" overclaims, because the Moon and Sun are ignored and that is not stated anywhere (I searched data.js and app.html).

**Also confirmed:** the earlier audit's suggestion (audit-final.json, flight timeout finding) to flag apoapsis beyond the Hill radius was not implemented. There is no Hill-radius check anywhere.

**Severity: minor.** The outputs are wrong or broken, but each one sits in a band about 0.001–0.004 decades wide, at absurd strengths (10^12 to 10^20 kg). That matches the earlier audit, which rated the analogous throw timeout minor because of how narrow it is.

**Fix tested** on a scratch copy (r15/repo, patch.js):
- calibration.js passes, sweep.js finds 0 problems across 5,184 contexts, and the 13.58 kaiju jump (263,676 km) is unchanged.
- Every repro above now reads "climbs past 1.5 × 10⁶ km, where the Sun's pull beats Earth's, and does not fall back", or gets the beyond-the-Moon caveat.

**Unrelated defect seen along the way:** the jump bulleted list says "He comes back down at 6,060 m/s, near terminal speed for a head-first fall (490 m/s)" for any kaiju arc from space. The landing speed is 12 times the terminal speed, so "near" is false. The sentence is gated only on apex > 20 m, not on the landing speed actually being close to terminal.

findings.title: 'Hurdle a twenty-story building' feat silently does nothing in real-muscle mode
findings.location: src/app.html runFeat lines 1143-1146
findings.evidence: Real muscle, click Simulate on 'Hurdle a twenty-story building' (card text: 'Runs the jump at the strength it needs (20 stories ≈ 60 m)'). The jump never reaches 60 m in real mode, so threshold() returns Infinity, the strength is left wherever it was (511 kg after the previous feat), and the page shows "Rex jumps 44 cm high." with no explanation.
findings.expected: A message that real muscle can't reach 60 m at any strength (the cap is about 6.9 m), or a switch to comic mode.
findings.fix: If kg is not finite, show a callout ('Real muscle tops out near X m; switch to Comic book to run this feat') or set state.mode = 'comic' before solving.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Chromium with preview.html, setting state through localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' and then clicking Simulate on the "Hurdle a twenty-story building" card. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/r16.js.
- Comic mode (the default): the strength is solved to logKg 5.2408 and the page shows "Rex jumps 60.1 m high". Works as advertised.
- Real mode at logKg 2.708 (511 kg, where the previous human feats leave it): logKg stays 2.708 and the page shows "Rex jumps 44 cm high. Ground holds (3.1% of limit)".
- Real mode at the default logKg 4.96: unchanged, "6.75 m".
- Real mode at 1e6 kg: "6.86 m". The real-muscle ceiling is about 11.6 m/s takeoff, so about 6.9 m, as the finding says.

Why it happens: in real mode the jump60 predicate is never true, so P.threshold returns Infinity. The `if (isFinite(kg))` guard then skips the strength update without telling the user, and only state.action changes. The card says "Runs the jump at the strength it needs (20 stories ≈ 60 m)", which is false in this state.

One correction to the finding: the panel is not completely unexplained. bayJump (app.html line 835) still shows its general note, "Real muscle caps his leg speed, so the jump tops out near 12 m/s of takeoff speed however strong he gets." But nothing links that note to the feat, and the 511 kg strength left over from an earlier feat produces a confusing 44 cm. This is a false claim on the card in a state users can reach but have to opt into (real muscle is not the default), so minor is the right severity.

The finding's suggested fix has a trap. runFeat applies `if (r.mode) state.mode = r.mode;` after the solve, and ctx() reads state.mode at solve time. So adding mode:'comic' to the feat's data alone would still solve in real mode and fail.

findings.title: All-Star Superman load is called '30 times the Moon's mass'. It is about 2.5 times
findings.location: build-data.py:173-174 (allstar liftNote) -> src/data.js:588; shown in Lift bay
findings.evidence: Repro: click Simulate on the '200 quintillion tons' feat, or set localStorage rex-lab-v1 = {logKg: log10(200e18*907.18474), action:'lift', obj:'allstar', surface:'concrete', mode:'comic'}. The Lift bay says: 'The comic never says what the load is. It is 30 times the Moon's mass, so treat it as a force equivalent.' Rendered and confirmed in Playwright.
findings.expected: 200e18 short tons × 907.18474 kg = 1.814e23 kg. The Moon is 7.346e22 kg (NASA NSSDC fact sheet, research moon_mass). Ratio = 2.47. The load is about 2.5 Moon masses, or about 3% of Earth's mass (1.814e23 / 5.972e24 = 0.030). '30 times' looks like the 0.030 Earth ratio misread.
findings.fix: In build-data.py, change the liftNote to: 'The comic never says what the load is. It is about 2.5 times the Moon's mass (3% of Earth's), so treat it as a force equivalent.' Then rebuild data.js and dist.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced the finding and could not refute it.

**Source text.** build-data.py:174, copied into src/data.js:588, dist/index.html:1740 and dist/preview.html:1740, reads: "The comic never says what the load is. It is 30 times the Moon’s mass, so treat it as a force equivalent."

**Browser run** (scratchpad/audit2/d1.js). I set localStorage rex-lab-v1 = {logKg: log10(200e18*907.18474), action:'lift', obj:'allstar', surface:'concrete', mode:'comic'} and reloaded dist/preview.html. The Lift bay shows that exact sentence. app.html:699 pushes o.liftNote into the bay. The "200 quintillion tons" feat card runs {action:'lift', obj:'allstar'}, so this is the state users reach by clicking that feat.

**Arithmetic, using the app's own data.js values:**
- allstar m = 200e18 × 907.18474 (ST, short ton) = 1.81437e23 kg
- Moon m = 7.346e22 kg (NSSDC, the source the page cites)
- Ratio to the Moon = 2.470
- Ratio to Earth = 1.814e23 / 5.9724e24 = 0.0304

The load is about 2.5 Moon masses. With metric or long tons it would be 2.72 or 2.77, so no reading of "tons" gets anywhere near 30. "30" is almost certainly the 0.030 Earth ratio misread as 30 Moon ratios.

**Is there a source for "30"?** None. research/final-fiction.json (all_star_superman_200_quintillion) gives only the 200-quintillion-ton figure and no Moon comparison.

**Severity: major.** The headline mass, 1.81e23 kg, is correct, so this is not critical. But the sentence is a false quantitative claim, off by a factor of 12, and it appears in a reachable state that a famous-feat button leads straight to. That fits the rubric's "wrong number/claim in a reachable state".

findings.title: The 'Canon' badge sits on three figures that are only reported by press or reviews
findings.location: build-data.py:69-74 (tiers secretwars/allstar/earth), :288-293 (feats); app.html:259 (definition); source table rows 'Strength: Hulk holds a mountain range', 'All-Star Superman', 'Superman benches Earth', 'Mass: Secret Wars…', 'Mass: All-Star…'
findings.evidence: The feats intro defines 'Canon means the number is printed in the story.' Three cards carry the Canon badge: 'Hulk holds up a mountain range' (150 billion tons), '200 quintillion tons' and 'Bench-pressing the planet'. Their research notes say: Secret Wars #4, 'canon_stated rests on this press attribution; the exact wording, speaker and page cannot be verified (no scan or transcript seen)'. All-Star #1, 'Exact panel wording, page, tester … cannot be verified', and 'it may be a force equivalent'. Superman #13 rests on a PopMatters review plus Screen Rant. Fetched sources: Screen Rant (Peters) says 'According to Reed Richards, the Hulk carried at least 150 billion tons'. Looper says 'holds up a weight of 200 quintillion tons' with no issue number. The tomwritesaboutstuff review says 'Superman is able to push 200 quintillion tons'. None of the three shows the panel. The cards hedge in their text, but the badge still claims the number is printed.
findings.expected: A status that says the figure is press-reported and the panel is unseen. Either add a 'Reported' status ('canon per press accounts; panel not seen') or show these three as 'Claimed'. Keep 'Canon' for figures confirmed in a scan or text (Action Comics #1 caption, OHOTMU handbook entries, Journey to the West).
findings.fix: In build-data.py, pass st='reported' (or 'claimed') for these three feats and tier rows. Add the label to statusLabel in app.html:1127. Extend the intro at app.html:259: 'Reported means comics press quotes the number but we could not see the page.'

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this. In the browser (dist/preview.html, default state, Famous feats section), the intro says "Canon means the number is printed in the story." Seven cards carry the CANON badge, including the three named: "Hulk holds up a mountain range" (Secret Wars #4, linked to Screen Rant), "200 quintillion tons" (All-Star Superman #1, linked to Looper) and "Bench-pressing the planet" (Superman vol. 3 #13, linked to PopMatters). In the Sources table, five rows show "canon stated": Strength: Hulk holds a mountain range, Strength: All-Star Superman, Strength: Superman benches Earth, Mass: Secret Wars mountain range and Mass: All-Star Superman's load.

The project's own research says nobody saw the page for any of the three:
- **Secret Wars #4** (final-fiction.json): "canon_stated rests on this press attribution; the exact wording, speaker and page cannot be verified (no scan or transcript seen)." Both verifier passes in verdicts-fiction.json say the same.
- **All-Star Superman #1:** "Exact panel wording, page, tester … cannot be verified." Placing it in issue #1 rests on a personal blog.
- **Superman vol. 3 #13:** rests on the PopMatters review plus Screen Rant.

My own web searches found no panel text for any of them. So the badge, as the page defines it, claims more than the site has checked.

**Why I rate it minor, not major:**
- **No number is shown wrong.** The figures are very likely official. On Internet Archive full-text search, Marvel's own Incredible Hulk #459 letters page reads "…the reference to SECRET WARS #4. The mountain did weigh in at about 150 billion tons." Marvel Previews vol. 6 #29 also prints "Beneath one hundred and fifty billion tons stands the Hulk." All press sources agree on 200 quintillion tons and "weight of the planet."
- **Two of the three cards disclose the sourcing next to the badge** ("per Reed Richards in press accounts", "Issue and exact wording come from reviews").

What is wrong is the evidence grade, which falls under misleading labelling.

**One aggravating detail.** The Bench-press card has no hedge at all. Its quote marks around "the weight of the planet" (card text, ladder tier line and source-table value) are PopMatters' paraphrase ("a machine that can exert the weight of the planet"), shown as if they were the comic's words. The All-Star card's "Three times more than before." is likewise the blogger's sentence.

**Side issue.** The definition "printed in the story" doesn't strictly fit the handbook entries that rightly keep Canon. The Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe is reference material, not story.

I dry-ran the fix below on a scratch copy of build-data.py. It changes exactly the 3 feats and 5 source rows above. Canon stays on Action Comics #1, Captain America, Class 100 and the Ruyi staff.
