findings.title: Quake uncertainty is given as '±1 magnitude' (actually ±0.67), and the quake magnitude is called an upper bound when it uses the central efficiency
findings.location: src/static-data.js:23 (assumption 'Blasts, quakes and craters are upper bounds'); src/app.html:874 (Stomp bay)
findings.evidence: Repro: Stomp on granite at logKg 12. The bay shows 'Quake: magnitude 2' and the line '…The real share ranges 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, so read it as ±1 magnitude.' The assumptions panel says the same, under a heading that calls quakes upper bounds. The engine computes M = (log10(E·1e-4) − 4.8)/1.5 (engine.js:532-537). Collins et al. 2005 (fetched PDF, Eq. 40*) gives M = 0.67 log10 E − 5.87, with efficiency 'one part in ten thousand … range between 10⁻⁵–10⁻³'.
findings.expected: A factor of 10 in seismic efficiency moves M by log10(10)/1.5 = 0.67. The range is ±⅔ magnitude, not ±1. Since 10⁻⁴ is the central value, the true magnitude could be 0.67 higher, so the quake number is not an upper bound.
findings.fix: Say 'read it as ±⅔ magnitude (about ±0.7)' in both places. Retitle the assumption 'Blasts and craters are upper bounds; quakes are central estimates', or similar.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Chromium using dist/preview.html with localStorage rex-lab-v1 = {logKg:12, mode:'comic', surface:'granite', action:'stomp'}. The page shows the chip 'Quake: magnitude 2' and the line 'Quake magnitude assumes 1 part in 10,000 ... The real share ranges 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, so read it as ±1 magnitude.' The assumptions panel has the heading 'Blasts, quakes and craters are upper bounds' and the text '(real range 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³: read ±1 magnitude)'.

The maths: engine.js:532-537 computes M = (log10(E·eff) − 4.8)/1.5, so dM/dlog10(eff) = 1/1.5 = 0.667. I ran it with E = 1 kt (4.184e12 J... actually 4.184e15 J input) and got M = 3.881 at eff 1e-5, 4.548 at 1e-4 and 5.214 at 1e-3, which is exactly ±0.667. The page's own sentence ('ranges 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, so ...') derives the band from the efficiency range, and that derivation gives ±⅔, not ±1.

The project's research file (research/final-environment.json, key seismic_efficiency_impact) quotes Collins et al. 2005: 1e-4 is 'the most commonly accepted figure ... with a range between 10⁻⁵–10⁻³'. So the quake uses a central value. A seismic efficiency of 1e-3 is just as plausible, which would put the magnitude 0.67 higher. Calling quakes an 'upper bound' is therefore false. Nothing else in stomp(), throw or jump makes the quake conservative: E is the impactor or foot kinetic energy, the same basis Collins uses.

Severity is minor rather than major. The headline magnitude itself is correct (it matches Collins Eq. 40* within 0.08). The error is in a secondary uncertainty statement, and it overstates the band, which errs on the cautious side. The 'upper bound' mislabel sits in a heading whose own text already presents the efficiency as a range. It is still a real inaccuracy and a dishonest label that an accuracy-focused critic would flag.

{ t: 'Blasts and craters are upper bounds; quakes are a middle estimate', d: 'Blast radii use the Kinney–Graham curve for TNT, as if all the energy became a blast. Quake magnitudes assume 1 part in 10,000 of the energy becomes shaking, the usual impact-study value (real range 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, so the true magnitude could be about ⅔ lower or higher). Craters use asteroid-impact scaling, which overstates small craters in rock or concrete.' }

findings.title: Superman vol. 3 #13: a reviewer's words are put in quotation marks as if printed in the comic
findings.location: build-data.py:73 (tier who) and :292 (feat claim) -> src/data.js:64, :987, :1261
findings.evidence: Card: 'A machine exerts “the weight of the planet” for him to bench.' Tier/dial: 'Superman vol. 3 #13 (2012): “the weight of the planet”'. The only source is PopMatters' review (fetched), which in its own words says 'she has a lab with a machine that can exert the weight of the planet for Superman to bench-press'. It has no quotation marks and attributes no text to the issue. The research marks the Screen Rant details as possibly the writer's own gloss.
findings.expected: No quotation marks, or attribute the wording to the review, e.g. 'A machine exerts the weight of the planet for him to bench (per PopMatters' review).'
findings.fix: Drop the curly quotes in the tier who, the feat claim and the source-row value, and add 'per a review'. The same applies to the All-Star card's “Three times more than before.”, which is the tomwritesaboutstuff reviewer's line ('That's three times more than before (!)'). It is disclosed, but would read better unquoted.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this, and it holds up. I ran Playwright on dist/preview.html with localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' = {logKg: log10(5.9724e24), action:'lift', obj:'earth'}. The page shows the phrase in curly quotes in three places:
1. The tier line reads "Superman benches Earth · Superman vol. 3 #13 (2012): “the weight of the planet”".
2. The famous-feat card reads "A machine exerts “the weight of the planet” for him to bench." under "Superman vol. 3 #13 · 2012".
3. The sources-table row "Strength: Superman benches Earth" shows the value "“the weight of the planet”".
These come from build-data.py:73 and :292 and appear in src/data.js:64, :987 and :1261.

The only source for that wording is the PopMatters review (Jay Mattson, 29 Oct 2012). I fetched it. The sentence is the reviewer's own narration: "Oh, and she has a lab with a machine that can exert the weight of the planet for Superman to bench-press." It has no quotation marks and attributes no words to the comic. The project's own research says the same: final-fiction.json and verdicts-fiction.json cite it as the review's text, and say Screen Rant's "six sextillion metric tonnes" may be Screen Rant's own gloss.

I tried to find the issue's actual wording to refute the finding. Searches of PopMatters, Comic Box Commentary, Screen Rant, Attack of the Fanboy and Comic Vine turned up no transcription of a caption or line of dialogue. Comic Box Commentary also paraphrases ("bench pressing the weight of the Earth"), with no quotes. So the quoted wording is not verified as the comic's.

Elsewhere on the page, curly quotes under an issue or work name mean the source's own text: Handbook “in excess of 100 tons”, Hesiod “Upholds the wide heaven…”, Captain America “As strong as a human can be.” The page has no note explaining its quoting style (grep of app.html for quot/verbatim/wording finds nothing). A reader will therefore take “the weight of the planet” as the comic's words, when it is a reviewer's paraphrase. That is mislabelled attribution. The number itself (Earth's mass, 5.9724e24 kg) is correctly sourced, so this is minor, not major.

The All-Star part of the finding also holds, but it is milder. “Three times more than before.” is the tomwritesaboutstuff reviewer's own sentence ("That's three times more than before (!) and counting!"), not a line from the comic. The card says "Issue and exact wording come from reviews", so it is disclosed, but quoting it still suggests comic dialogue.

One more small point: the earth tier note quotes the phrase differently (“Weight of a planet”) from the who line (“the weight of the planet”), so the page quotes two wordings for one phrase.

Edit build-data.py, not the generated files, then regenerate src/data.js and dist.

1. Line 73 (earth tier):

findings.title: Saitama card claims 'Clears the sky over the planet', which neither the research nor the cited source supports
findings.location: build-data.py:294 -> src/data.js:1003
findings.evidence: The research fact saitama_serious_punch only says the punch defeated Boros and that his abilities are 'limitless'. The linked Wikipedia page (fetched) does not describe any effect on clouds or sky. Fan sources disagree on the scope ('large portion of the globe' vs 'entire planet').
findings.expected: Every claim on a card should be in its cited source. Either cite the anime episode or manga chapter for the cloud-splitting shot, or drop it.
findings.fix: Change to 'Defeats Boros with one punch. No number is ever given; fan estimates are not canon.' Or add a research fact with an episode/chapter citation that shows the clouds split.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this and tried to refute it. The labelling problem is real. The claim is not invented, but it is overstated.

**What the page shows.** I loaded dist/preview.html in Playwright and read the feat card that mentions Saitama. It says: "Saitama's Serious Punch / One-Punch Man · 2015 / Clears the sky over the planet. No number is ever given; fan estimates are not canon. / NOT QUANTIFIED / Source". The only link is https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saitama_(One-Punch_Man). The text comes from build-data.py:294 and appears in src/data.js:1003, dist/index.html and dist/preview.html. Through feat() (build-data.py:254-259), the card links only the first source of its research fact.

**What the cited source says.** I fetched that Wikipedia article. None of the words cloud, clouds, sky, atmosphere or planet appear in it. It only says the serious punch defeated "the world-conquering leader of the aliens, Lord Boros" and calls his power "limitless" and "immeasurable". The second research source, List of One-Punch Man episodes, gives only the title and air date for S1E12, with no summary. In research/final-fiction.json, the saitama_serious_punch fact has nothing about clouds or the sky either. Both verdict files (verdicts-fiction.json) confirmed only the Boros defeat and the absence of any number. So nothing in the project's research supports the sky sentence.

**Why it isn't a fabrication.** The canon work does show a cloud effect. The fandom wiki's "Killer Move: Serious Series" page, which I pulled through its API, says the shockwave "was also strong enough to part clouds across the globe". It cites manga ch. 36, p. 68-69, and anime episode 12. A web search found TV Tropes describing it as "a massive gap in the sky that stretches through the circumference of the planet". I couldn't load TV Tropes directly (HTTP 403), so I have that wording only from the search summary.

**Why it is still a defect.**
- The card's only link does not support its main sentence. On a page whose selling point is honest sourcing, a reader who clicks "Source" finds nothing about the sky.
- The wording goes further than canon. Canon shows clouds parted in a band around the globe. "Clears the sky over the planet" reads as the whole sky over the whole planet being cleared.

**Severity: minor.** This is misleading wording and unsupported labelling on one feat card. It is not a wrong number, and it doesn't affect a computed result.
verdict.better_fix:
Simplest fix, which uses only what the cited source supports. Change build-data.py:294 to:
    feat('comic', 'Saitama’s Serious Punch', 'One-Punch Man · 2015', 'Defeats Boros with one punch. No number is ever given; fan estimates are not canon.', ['saitama_serious_punch'],
Then regenerate src/data.js and dist/ the usual way.

Alternative, if you want to keep the cloud image: make the wording match canon and name where it appears. For example: 'His punch’s shockwave parts the clouds around the globe (manga ch. 36; anime S1E12). No number is ever given; fan estimates are not canon.' Then add a source for it to the saitama_serious_punch fact in research/final-fiction.json, and list it first so the card's "Source" link points to it: {"title": "One-Punch Man Wiki: Serious Series (cites ch. 36 p. 68-69, ep. 12)", "url": "https://onepunchman.fandom.com/wiki/Killer_Move:_Serious_Series"}. Do not keep "clears the sky over the planet" with only the Wikipedia link.

findings.title: 'Superman catches a 777' runs at Hulk strength (90.7 t), which cannot hold a 247 t 777
findings.location: build-data.py:286-287 (run liftKg=100*ST, obj='b777')
findings.evidence: Clicking Simulate makes the Lift bay headline read 'Rex can't budge it. It needs 2.7× more strength. Strength: 37% of what's needed' (Playwright, concrete, comic). The card promises a catch: 'Watch what his hands do to the fuselage.'
findings.expected: The run should use at least the 777's weight (247.2 t) so the catch happens and the grip failure (40× what the skin can take) is the story.
findings.fix: Set run liftKg to about 2.5e5 (or 247200×1.1). Or add to the card: 'At Hulk's 100 tons he can't even hold it.'

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this myself and could not refute it.

**Data.** build-data.py:286-287 gives the "Superman catches a 777" card `run=dict(liftKg=100 * ST, action='lift', obj='b777')`. That is 90,718 kg, the same value as the Hulk/Thor "Class 100" card on the line above, so it looks like a copy-paste. src/data.js:946-949 carries `liftKg: 90718.474` to the page. The b777 object weighs 247,200 kg (build-data.py:143).

**Engine.** `lift()` (engine.js:581) sets `canLift = ctx.F >= W`. 90,718 / 247,200 = 0.367, so canLift is false.

**Browser.** I ran a Playwright script (scratchpad/audit2/d8.js) on dist/preview.html and clicked the card's Simulate button. That stored state `{logKg: 4.9577, action: 'lift', obj: 'b777', surface: 'concrete'}` and the page showed:
- Strength dial: "Lifts 90.7 t … Hulk & Thor (Class 100) · Official Handbook (1986)". That is a Hulk label on a Superman card.
- Verdict: "Rex can't budge it. It needs 2.7× more strength."
- Status: "Strength: 37% of what's needed | Below: what would happen if he could".

The card itself says "A 777-200 weighs up to 247 t … Watch what his hands do to the fuselage." So the preset contradicts its own card. The catch never happens, and the grip failure appears only as a hypothetical meter ("hand pressure vs. what the 777 can take: 40× the limit").

**What correct looks like.** To catch and hold the plane, Rex needs at least m·g of a 247.2 t 777-200 at max takeoff weight (the Wikipedia specs already in the sources table). I set logKg = log10(247200 × 1.1) = log10(271,920) through localStorage (scratchpad/audit2/d8fix.js). The page then reads:
- Verdict: "Rex has the strength. The ground and the 777 don't."
- Status: "Strength: 1.1× what's needed | Ground fails: 11× its limit | Grip: crushes the 777"
- Happens list: "His palms press 80.8 MPa into the 777, which gives way at about 2 MPa…"

That is the fuselage story the card promises. At 2.5e5 kg the status reads "1× what's needed", which looks odd, so 1.1× is the better choice.

**Why minor.** The physics shown is correct for the strength that was set. Nothing false is claimed about the world, and the grip meter still appears under "what would happen if he could". The defect is a preset that does not match its card: the headline contradicts the card's premise and the dial shows a Hulk label on a Superman feat. That is mislabelling that hurts comprehension on one feat card, not a wrong headline physics number.
verdict.better_fix: In /home/user/dino-strength-sim/build-data.py:287, change the run to `run=dict(liftKg=247200 * 1.1, action='lift', obj='b777')`. If you prefer to read the mass from the `objects` list (line 128), use that object's `m` × 1.1. Then regenerate src/data.js and dist. This sets the dial to 272 t, about 1.1× the 777-200's 247.2 t max takeoff weight. Rex holds the plane, and the page shows "Rex has the strength. The ground and the 777 don't." with "Grip: crushes the 777" (80.8 MPa against about 2 MPa). Keep the margin above exactly 247,200: at about 2.5e5 the status prints "1× what's needed", and an exact value risks falling below the canLift threshold when converted to logKg and back.

findings.title: Feat status badges are inconsistent and the intro defines them wrongly
findings.location: build-data.py:254-257 (feat status = max rank over all keys); app.html:259 (intro); app.html:1127
findings.evidence: (a) 'Spider-Man lifts 10 tons' shows 'Estimate' because its keys include marvel_handbook_ton_unit (estimate). The research confirms the 10-ton figure is printed (Deluxe #12 scan, fetched: 'lift (press) approximately 10 tons'). 'Hulk and Thor: Class 100' uses the same short-ton reading and shows 'Canon'. (b) The intro never defines 'Estimate', which two cards use. (c) The intro says 'Verified means a sanctioned record', but Bolt's 12.42 m/s card is a 20 m split average from a biomechanics paper (Coh 2019), not a sanctioned record.
findings.expected: Badge the card by its primary fact (the printed 10 tons is Canon), define every badge used, and word Verified as 'measured or officially recorded and checked against the source'.
findings.fix: In feat(), set status from keys[0] only unless st is given. Add 'Estimate means our own reading or calculation' to the intro, and reword the Verified definition.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced all three parts. I loaded src/data.js in Node and rendered dist/preview.html in Chromium, reading each card's badge text from #feat-groups and taking a screenshot (scratchpad/audit2/d9-feats.png).

(a) Spider-Man's 10 tons is printed, but its card says "Estimate".
- The "Spider-Man lifts 10 tons" card shows ESTIMATE. feat() in build-data.py:254-258 sets the status to the worst rank across all keys. This card's keys are spider_man_handbook_1986 (canon_stated) and marvel_handbook_ton_unit (estimate).
- The research fact spider_man_handbook_1986 is canon_stated and quotes Deluxe #12: "lift (press) approximately 10 tons". So the number in the title is printed.
- The card "Hulk and Thor: Class 100" uses the same short-ton reading (its liftKg is 100*ST) but lists only canon keys, so it shows CANON.
- "Sun Wukong's staff" also converts units (jin at 590 g) and shows CANON.
- The page contradicts itself: the Sources table row "Strength: Spider-Man | ~10 tons" is canon_stated.
- I checked every multi-key feat. Only Spider-Man changes status under the worst-rank rule:
  - 777: keys[0] is not_quantified, the overall result is the same.
  - Samson: keys[0] is not_quantified, the overall result is the same.
  - Hulk and Thor: both keys are canon.

(b) The intro never defines "Estimate". Its text is: "Verified means a sanctioned record. Canon means the number is printed in the story. Claimed or disputed means nobody can check it. Not quantified means..." Two cards still show ESTIMATE: "The car on the cover" and "Spider-Man lifts 10 tons".

(c) "Verified means a sanctioned record" is too narrow.
- Bolt's "Top speed 12.42 m/s" card is VERIFIED. Its fact bolt_peak_running_speed says it is a 60-80 m split average from Coh 2019 / Graubner & Nixdorf 2011, "not an instantaneous laser peak". No body ratifies top speeds, so this is a biomechanics measurement, not a sanctioned record.
- Chapman's 105.8 mph pitch (VERIFIED) is likewise a radar or tracking reading, not a sanctioned record.
- The data is right; the label definition is what misleads.

Severity minor: these are badge and wording errors that mislead about how solid a number is. No figure is wrong.
verdict.better_fix:
1) build-data.py:282. Do not let a unit convention set the badge. Either drop the unit key, which matches the Hulk/Thor card: feat('comic', 'Spider-Man lifts 10 tons', ..., ['spider_man_handbook_1986'], run=...) or keep the key and pin the status with st='canon_stated'. The claim text already says "Handbook tons are read here as US short tons", so the inference stays labelled. I prefer this targeted change over making feat() use keys[0] only. The worst-rank rule is a sensible conservative default for other cards, and the actual defect is listing a unit-convention fact as a status key. findings.title: Air-heating row says the table 'matches Anderson's 11 km/s textbook case within ~2%', but the table's own value at 11 km/s is 16,435 K
findings.location: build-data.py:247; engine.js:286-292 comment
findings.evidence: stagnationT(11000) = 16,435 K (test/calibration.js prints it). Anderson's Apollo case is about 11,600 K at about 1 atm. The earlier audit (audit-final.json) says it was the solver run at 1 atm that gave 11,777 K, and that the textbook value was 'recalled from memory'. The table is built at sea-level stagnation pressure (ρ0·v² ≈ 1,500 atm), so its values cannot match Anderson's case. The row also has no citation for Anderson.
findings.expected: For example: 'equilibrium-air solver (reproduces Anderson's ~11,600 K Apollo shock-layer case at ~1 atm within 2%); table evaluated at sea-level stagnation pressure'. Add a citation, e.g. Anderson, Hypersonic and High-Temperature Gas Dynamics.
findings.fix: Reword the row value and the engine comment, and add the citation as extra_sources.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute D12 and could not. The finding is real, and minor is the right severity.

**What the page says.** I opened dist/preview.html in Playwright and read the 'Air heating' row of the sourced-numbers table. It says: 'Above: equilibrium-air table computed for this sim (dissociation and ionization included; matches Anderson's 11 km/s textbook case within ~2%; radiation ignored, so an upper bound)'. The row has three sources: NASA BGH stagtmp, NASA BGH realgas and CAIB §3.6. None of them is Anderson. The engine comment at src/engine.js:286-289 says the table was 'computed for this project at sea-level stagnation pressure; it matches Anderson's 11 km/s textbook case to about 2%'.

**What the engine gives.** In Node:
- `stagnationT(11000)` = 16,435 K.
- 7 km/s = 9,836 K, 10 km/s = 14,060 K, 15 km/s = 27,313 K.
- The ideal-gas value at 11 km/s is 60,507 K.

**The textbook case.** Anderson (2006), *Hypersonic and High-Temperature Gas Dynamics* 2nd ed., gives the Apollo case as M∞ = 32.5 at 53 km (11 km/s): 58,128 K for a perfect gas against about 11,600 K for the real gas. I confirmed these figures through the meteor shock-wave review arXiv 1805.07842, which quotes them from Anderson 2006. The NATO STO EN-AVT-116-03 note gives the same flight condition (53 km, 11 km/s, M 32.5). So the number is real; the earlier audit did not misremember it. I also checked the book's DOI: 10.2514/4.861956 resolves through Crossref to the Anderson Jr. 2nd edition, 2006.

**My reproduction.** I wrote audit2/d12/d12_check.py, which drives the earlier audit's Gibbs equilibrium-air solver (audit/f7refute/eqair.py):

| Pressure | T at 11 km/s | vs 11,600 K |
|---|---|---|
| ~0.84 atm (post-shock at 53 km, ρ ≈ 7e-4) | 11,676 K | +0.7% |
| 1 atm | 11,777 K | +1.5% |
| Sea-level stagnation, ρ₀v² ≈ 1,463 atm (the table's condition) | 16,602 K | +43% |

The engine's table entry for 11 km/s is 16,435 K, or +42%.

**Conclusion.**
- The '~2%' holds only for the solver run at about 1 atm. The table the row describes is built at about 1,500 times that pressure, where dissociation is suppressed, and is about 42% above Anderson's value.
- The table itself is physically fine for sea-level air. Only the label is false.
- A reader who checks the claim will find 16,400 K against 11,600 K, and the claim has no citation.
- This is misleading wording in the assumptions/sources table, not a wrong headline number, so it is minor.

**Separate defect found while checking (not part of D12; it is major and needs its own finding).** Every row's Sources cell in the sourced-numbers table renders as plain text such as ',https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/BGH/stagtmp.html · ,https://...'. There are no link titles and no clickable links.
- Repro: open dist/preview.html and read `#src-table tbody tr td:nth-child(4)` innerHTML.
- Cause: src/app.html:1167 (dist/index.html:5053) passes `.map(...)`, which returns an array of `[sep, <a>]` pairs. `el()` only does `kids.flat()` one level, so each pair is turned into a string, and an anchor element's string form is its href.
- Fix: change `.map(` to `.flatMap(` on that line. I verified it on a scratch copy (audit2/d12/preview_fix.html): the cell then renders as titled `<a>` links separated by ' · '.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/d12/: d12_check.py, ui2.js, ui3.js and ui4.js.

findings.title: Assumption 'real sites vary by 2–3×' understates the research ranges
findings.location: src/static-data.js:22
findings.evidence: The research ranges the sim draws on: granite 0.1–4 GPa against 1.7 GPa used (jointed rock is 17× lower), ice 5–25 MPa (5×), asphalt 1–5 MPa (5×), concrete slab 1.5–7.2 MPa, dense gravel 120–650 kPa.
findings.expected: 'Real sites vary by 2–5×; jointed rock can be 10× weaker than intact granite.'

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this two ways. My scratch script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/d13.js. I also loaded dist/preview.html in Playwright with default settings.

What the page says: the Assumptions "Ground" card reads "Typical ultimate bearing capacities; real sites vary by 2–3×." The text comes from src/static-data.js:22 and appears verbatim in src/data.js and dist/index.html.

What contradicts it: the page's own sources table (present in the rendered textContent) lists these research ranges, from research/final-environment.json:
- Loose sand: 37 kPa (22–73). That is 1.7× down and 2.0× up from the value used.
- Dense gravel: 241 kPa (118–650). 2.0× down, 2.7× up; the full range spans 5.5×.
- Soft clay: 129 kPa (77–296). 1.7× down, 2.3× up.
- Stiff clay: 482 kPa (308–1110). 1.6× down, 2.3× up.
- Asphalt: 2.5 MPa (1–5). 2.5× down, 2× up.
- Concrete slab: 2.5 MPa (1.5–7.2). 1.7× down, 2.9× up.
- Ice: the engine uses 5 MPa, the bottom of the research range (5–25 MPa). Real ice can be up to 5× stronger than the value used.
- Granite: the engine uses 1.7 GPa against a research range of 0.1–4.1 GPa. The low end, 100 MPa, is "jointed or weathered rock at about its UCS", which is 17× weaker. The full range spans 41×. The research note adds that "real outcrops are jointed and joints often govern", so the low end is the common case for real rock, not a rare one.
- Steel deck: no range is given.

Read generously, "vary by 2–3×" means "within a factor of 2–3 of the typical value either way". On that reading the claim holds for the six soil, pavement and slab surfaces. It fails for granite (17× down) and for ice (5× up from the value used). Read as the spread from weakest to strongest site, it fails for every surface (3.3× to 41×).

Granite is a selectable surface, so the claim does matter. The strength at which Rex punches through a granite floor, or launches off it, could really be about 17× lower than the sim shows. The page tells readers the uncertainty is only 2–3×, while its own collapsed sources table shows 0.1–4 GPa.

This is not a wrong headline number, and the sources table does disclose the ranges. So it is minor: misleading uncertainty wording that the page's own data contradicts. The fix the finding proposes ("jointed rock can be 10× weaker") would itself understate the research: 1.7 GPa / 0.1 GPa = 17×.

findings.title: Assumption wording doesn't match the engine on force shares and Hill curvature
findings.location: src/static-data.js:14 and :17
findings.evidence: (a) 'Every other move uses a share of it'. In Real muscle mode, the jump drives with 1.4× the dial force (engine.js:57 forceFrac 1.4, with a comment explaining why). The two-handed shove reaches 1.046× before it is capped. (b) 'Real muscle follows the Hill force–velocity curve (a/F₀ = 0.25)'. The research (hill_curvature_a_over_F0, status estimate) calls 0.25 a single-muscle convention and gives a whole-limb, multi-joint a/F₀ of 1.06 ± 0.72 (near-linear), warning 'expect a much flatter curve at whole-limb level'. findings.fix: For (a): 'Every other move uses a set fraction of it (a real-muscle jump gets 1.4×, because the legs also carry his own weight, which a deadlift record leaves out).' For (b): 'a/F₀ = 0.25, the single-muscle convention; whole limbs measure flatter'.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced both parts and could not refute either one.

(a) In src/engine.js:57 the real-muscle jump uses `jump: { vmax: 12, forceFrac: 1.4 }`, and actionForce() at line 578 returns ctx.F × forceFrac. So in Real muscle mode the jump drives with 1.4 times the dial force. The other moves stay at or below 1×. The two-handed shove's 2 × 0.523 = 1.046 is clamped by Math.min(ctx.F, …) at line 620, so in practice only the jump goes over. The comic jump's comicFrac is 0.66.

I ran it in the browser: dist/preview.html with localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' = {logKg: log10(511), inf: false, mode: 'real', action: 'jump', groundHolds: true}, and opened the <details>. The page shows both of these:
- Dial: "5.01 kN of force (2.8× his body weight)"
- Jump math: "Legs push his body (175 kg) up and his feet (5.2 kg) down with 7.02 kN over 0.5 m."

The Assumptions panel says "That times g is his maximum force. Every other move uses a share of it." So the page contradicts itself in a reachable state (Real muscle mode plus Jump).

The 1.4× itself is defensible. A deadlift record counts only the bar, but the leg extensors also push the body (511 kg + about 170 kg of body ≈ 1.33×), and the value was fitted to jump data (engine comment at lines 55-56). The page just never says so.

(b) MUSCLE.k = 0.25 (engine.js:50) is applied through hill() and pushApartHill() to the endpoint speed of whole-limb pushes (throws, punch, clap, jump, stomp). research/final-humans.json, entry hill_curvature_a_over_F0 (status "estimate"), gives this, quoted: "0.25 is a widely used normalization convention, not a measured human population mean", and for the multi-joint leg press "mean a/F0 1.06 +/- 0.72 ... authors prefer a linear model". It ends: "Use about 0.25 for single muscles and expect a much flatter curve at whole-limb level."

The Assumptions text ("Real muscle follows the Hill force–velocity curve (a/F₀ = 0.25)") presents 0.25 as the fact for real muscle. The sources-table row ("(F + a)(v + b) = (F₀ + a) b, a/F₀ = 0.25", ESTIMATE, note null) adds no caveat either.

The headline claim that limb speed tops out still holds for any curvature, and nothing the user reads as a number is shown wrong. Both problems are about disclosure and labelling, so minor is the right severity. Part (a) is at the top of minor because the page visibly shows 7.02 kN next to a stated 5.01 kN "maximum".

findings.title: 'Hurdle a twenty-story building' Simulate silently does nothing to strength in Real muscle mode
findings.location: src/app.html runFeat (~line 1142); build-data.py:276-277
findings.evidence: Repro: Settings → Real muscle, then click Simulate on 'Hurdle a twenty-story building'. P.threshold(jump apex ≥ 60 m) returns Infinity, because the real-muscle jump caps at about 6.9 m apex (jump at 1e30 N gives an apex of 6.86 m). runFeat skips the strength change, so the bay shows a jump at whatever strength was already set. The card promises 'Runs the jump at the strength it needs (20 stories ≈ 60 m)'.
findings.expected: The run should switch to comic mode, or say that real muscle cannot reach 60 m.
findings.fix: Add mode:'comic' to this feat's run, or show a callout when the solve returns Infinity.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in the engine and in the browser.

**Engine** (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/d16.js, d16b.js)
- The runFeat predicate (apex ≥ 60 m, escaped or relativistic) is solved with P.threshold over F = 10g to 1e45 N.
- At the default 2 m body in real mode it returns Infinity on every surface, every anchor and both ground settings.
- The real-muscle jump plateaus there: apex 6.864 m and v 11.65 m/s on comic ground, and 0.57–10.2 m on breakable ground.
- Comic mode always solves to a finite value: 36 t on rigid ground, 174 t on the default concrete, at most 288 t on sand.
- Real mode does solve once Rex is about 10 m or taller with comic ground, or 50 m or taller on concrete (e.g. H=50 gives 1.41e8 kg). So the failure depends on size, but it covers the default size and the 40 cm plush.

**Browser** (dist/preview.html, d16pw.js; Real muscle seeded in localStorage, then Simulate clicked on "Hurdle a twenty-story building")
- Start at 511 kg: localStorage logKg stays 2.708 and only action changes to 'jump'. The bay says "Rex jumps 44 cm high."
- Start at 1e20 kg: the strength is unchanged and the bay says "Rex jumps 6.86 m high".
- Start at ∞: the strength stays ∞ and the bay says "Rex leaves at light speed".
- In all three cases nothing mentions the 60 m target or says it can't be reached. The only hint is the generic line "Real muscle caps his leg speed, so the jump tops out near 12 m/s…".
- The same click in Comic mode works: strength goes to 174 t and the bay says "Rex jumps 60.1 m high".
- So the card's promise ("Runs the jump at the strength it needs (20 stories ≈ 60 m)") is false whenever Real muscle is on at default size, and the button does nothing to strength without saying so.

**Severity:** I confirm minor, borderline major. Real muscle is not the default. Every number the page shows is correct for the state it shows, and the real-muscle cap is mentioned in the bay. The defect is a silent no-op plus a card claim that is false in that mode.

**The finding's first fix is wrong.** Adding mode:'comic' to the run data alone does not work. runFeat applies r.mode (line 1148) after the solve (lines 1143–1147), so the solve still runs in real mode, gets Infinity and leaves strength untouched. Then the mode flips to comic. I tested this in a patched copy (fixA.html): at 2 m the page switches to Comic but stays at 511 kg and shows "Rex jumps 44 cm high", which is worse. At H=50 it solves in real mode and then flips to comic, giving 75.6 m instead of 60 m.

**Side issue (separate defect, not this finding):** at ∞ in Real muscle, P.jump returns v = c ("light speed (to the last digit)"). The same bay still says real muscle tops out near 12 m/s. At 1e45 N it correctly returns 11.65 m/s, so the infinite branch skips the real-muscle cap.

findings.title: Overclaiming labels: 'Half of people killed' and 'the fastest pitch ever thrown'
findings.location: build-data.py:190 (energy short), :211 (overpressure label)
findings.evidence: (a) The blast chart labels 427 kPa 'Half of people killed'. The research note on blast_lethality_threshold says 'Primary blast only; debris and whole-body displacement kill at far lower pressures.' The chart also puts 'Houses collapse' at a radius 3–4× larger. (b) compareEnergy prints e.g. '2.4× the fastest pitch ever thrown' (Stomp at 511 kg). The research and Guinness support 'fastest recorded'. Pitches before radar are unknown.
findings.expected: (a) 'Half killed by the pressure wave alone'. (b) 'the fastest pitch on record'.
findings.fix: Edit the two strings in build-data.py and rebuild.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced both parts in Chromium using dist/preview.html with localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' set.

(a) Blast label. Settings {action:'punch', logKg:9} give the bars "Windows shatter 62.4 m, Houses collapse 24.3 m, Eardrums start to burst 21.2 m, Lung damage 13.9 m, Half of people killed 6.81 m". {action:'clap', logKg:12} gives "...Houses collapse 288 m ... Half of people killed 80.5 m". The 427 kPa value comes from research/final-environment.json, key blast_lethality_threshold: Glasstone & Dolan 1977, Table 12.38, 50% lethality from direct blast, 62 psi. The research note there says: "Primary blast only; debris and whole-body displacement kill at far lower pressures." No string on the page carries that caveat (grep for primary, direct, pressure wave and debris in app.html, data.js and static-data.js finds nothing). So the chart presents 6.81 m as the radius where half the people die, while its own "Houses collapse" bar (26.8 kPa) reaches 3.6 times farther. For comparison, the usual combined-effects figures (OTA 1979) put about 50% killed at 5–12 psi (34–83 kPa), not 62 psi. The real 50% fatality radius from all causes is several times larger. Read on its own, the label understates the lethal zone by leaving out its qualifier. This is honest-labelling wording, so minor.

(b) Pitch wording. Settings {action:'stomp', logKg:log10(511)} show "Compared with: 2.4× the fastest pitch ever thrown". Clap shows "2.2× ..." and punch "≈ the fastest pitch ever thrown". The sources say "recorded": Guinness "Fastest baseball pitch (male)" (Statcast) and SABR "fastest pitch ever recorded". Pitches before radar were never measured, and early radar readings were taken near the plate, not at release (Ryan's 1974 100.9 mph is one example). "Ever thrown" claims more than the sources support. Minor.

Correction to the proposed fix: the auditor's label "Half killed by the pressure wave alone" (38 chars) breaks the phone layout. In logBars, padL is capped at w*0.5. At a 375 px viewport the chart is 309 px wide, and I measured that label's text starting at x = -104, so "Half killed by the" is clipped off the left edge. Long labels need to stay at 21 characters or fewer. "Eardrums start to burst" already clips by 5 px; that is separate and not part of this finding. "Pressure kills half" (19 chars) measured x = 22 at 375 px with no clipping. The qualifier belongs in the chart caption, which wraps freely.
verdict.better_fix:
In build-data.py, then rebuild data.js/dist:
1) line 190: short='the fastest pitch on record'  (compareEnergy then prints "2.4× the fastest pitch on record").
2) line 211: dict(id='lethal', label='Pressure kills half', Pa=427000, k='blast_lethality_threshold'),   (19 chars, so it fits the 309 px phone chart. The suggested 'Half killed by the pressure wave alone' is clipped by about 104 px at a 375 px viewport.)
3) In src/app.html blastBlock(), add the caveat to the caption. Change
  'Upper bound: real moves couple far less energy into air than explosives do.'
to
  'Upper bound: real moves couple far less energy into air than explosives do. Injury and death levels count the pressure wave alone (Glasstone & Dolan); flying debris and collapsing buildings kill much farther out.'

findings.title: The slider end label says 10³⁴ kg is "heavier than 10,000 Suns". It is about 5,000 Suns.
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:198 (.scale-ends, directly under the strength slider)
findings.evidence: Every load at 390 and 1280, in both themes, shows "10³⁴ kg (heavier than 10,000 Suns)" under the strength slider (screenshot lay_fold-390-light.png). The slider max is 34, which means 1e34 kg.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this and could not refute it. The slider in /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:197 is `<input type="range" id="strength" min="1" max="34">`, and its value is log10(kg). The app reads it with `state.logKg = Number(e.target.value)` (line 500) and computes force as `Math.pow(10, state.logKg) * g` (line 430). LMAX = 34 (line 1017), and the "10 kg" label at min=1 follows the same mapping. So the right end of the slider really is 1e34 kg.

The project's own data puts the Sun at 1.9884e30 kg (data.js:487, "Mass: The Sun", status verified, NASA NSSDCA fact sheet). That gives 1e34 / 1.9884e30 = 5,029 Suns (5,029 with the IAU nominal 1.98847e30 too). "Heavier than 10,000 Suns" is false by a factor of about 2. The slider would have to reach about 10^34.3 kg (1.99e34) for the claim to hold.

I loaded dist/preview.html in Chromium (Playwright, 390x844), and `.scale-ends span` contains `['10 kg', '10³⁴ kg (heavier than 10,000 Suns)']` with slider max = 34. The label is static markup at app.html:198 and is copied unchanged into dist/index.html:198. It shows on every load, directly under the main control, at every width. It contradicts the page's own sourced Sun mass. For an owner who cares most about factual accuracy, this meets the rubric's "false claim most users will see", so critical stands. It is a label rather than a computed result, but it is a visible, checkably false claim on the first screen.
verdict.better_fix: In /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html line 198, change `10³⁴ kg (heavier than 10,000 Suns)` to `10³⁴ kg (about 5,000 Suns)` Then rebuild dist with `node /home/user/dino-strength-sim/build.js` and the preview with `node /home/user/dino-strength-sim/test/shots.js`, so dist/index.html:198 picks up the change. An alternative that keeps "10,000 Suns" true is to raise LMAX and the slider max to 34.3, but that changes engine range and test expectations. The text fix is smaller and safer.

findings.title: Tapping a ladder dot sets the strength of a different marker
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:1081-1086 (each marker group adds a transparent hit rect x = left ? 0 : axisX, width axisX, on its label row; groups are drawn in sequence, so later rects cover earlier dots, and right-hand rects start exactly at the axis)
findings.evidence: Touch emulation at 390x844, starting from 10^1.5 kg: tapping the Spider-Man dot gives the dial "Lifts 300 t" (Jump clears the Statue of Liberty). The Hulk & Thor dot gives "Lifts 561 t" (Fist breaks the sound barrier). The Strongest-human dot gives "Lifts 363 kg · Captain America". At 1280, elementFromPoint at the dot centres resolves 7 of 18 dots to another marker. The intro promises "Tap any marker to jump there."

findings.fix: Draw all hit rects in a first pass, then the circles in a second pass on top, each with its own transparent r=11 hit circle that triggers that marker. Start right-hand rects at axisX+10 and end left-hand rects at axisX-10.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Playwright, in both the built dist/preview.html and the src/app.html code (dist line 4972 matches src line 1086). Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/: l03.js does the reproduction and l03-verify.js checks the patched copy.

Cause: each marker group <g class="mk"> ends with a transparent hit rect, `x: left ? 0 : axisX, width: axisX, y: it.ty-14, height: 32`. That rect covers the axis column, the dot centre x=axisX included. The groups are appended one after another, tiers first and then thresholds, each sorted top to bottom. So a later group's label-row rect sits on top of an earlier group's dot whenever the label rows overlap that dot's y. Right-hand rects start exactly at axisX, so threshold rows also take tier dots. Every right-hand row hits from the axis outward, so the threshold groups also swallow the right half of tier dots.

Results with state {logKg:1.5, inf:false}:
- elementFromPoint at the dot centres: 8 of 18 dots resolve to a different marker at 1280x900, and 4 of 18 at 390x844.
- Real clicks at 1280: Superman benches Earth dot gives "Lifts 181 quintillion t" (All-Star Superman); Hulk & Thor gives "Lifts 561 t" (sound barrier); Spider-Man and Back-lift record both give "Lifts 300 t" (Statue of Liberty jump); Strongest human gives "Lifts 363 kg | Captain America"; Hulk Secret Wars gives "Lifts 150 billion t" (Hiroshima); the "Fist breaks the sound barrier" dot gives 300 t (the Jump leader path catches the exact centre).
- Touch taps at 390 (hasTouch/isMobile): Hulk & Thor gives 561 t, Spider-Man 300 t, Strongest human 363 kg · Captain America, Hulk Secret Wars 150 billion t.

Tapping Spider-Man shows "Lifts 300 t ≈ 587× the strongest human" with no name, so a reader may take 300 t as Spider-Man's figure. Tapping the default "Strongest human" dot puts Captain America's 363 kg on the dial. Hover tooltips have the same wrong mapping, since pointerenter fires on the covering group. This is broken UI in a prominent, reachable section, so major is correct.

The proposed fix would not fully work. A second pass of r=11 hit circles on top still routes wrongly where dots almost coincide. Hulk Secret Wars (10^14.134 kg) and the Hiroshima threshold (10^14.176) are about 1 px apart. Strongest human (10^2.708) and Captain America (10^2.560) are 3.3 px apart at 1280 and 3.8 px at 390. A later-drawn r=11 circle captures both. The hit targets have to be split by axis side and by the midpoint between neighbouring dots on the same side. I patched a copy (scratchpad/audit2/preview-fixed2.html) with the change below. All 18 dots and all 18 labels then set their own strength at both 1280 (mouse) and 390 (touch): 0 mismatches. The unpatched page has 4 and 2 even with taps offset 2.5 px toward the marker's own side, and 8 and 4 at the exact centres.

findings.title: The launch-angle slider cannot be dragged: the bay re-render swaps out the input mid-drag

findings.evidence: Throw tab at 1280: dragging the thumb with the mouse from 45° toward about 9° in 20 moves ends at "Launch angle: 43°". The original input node is detached (isConnected=false) 30 ms into the drag. At 390, a touch drag (CDP touch events) from 45° toward about 9° ends at 39°. Arrow keys still work, because focus is restored by id.

findings.fix: In renderBay, when an element with the same id as document.activeElement (or the element under pointer capture) exists in the new parts, move the old live node into the new tree (newEl.replaceWith(oldEl)). Alternatively, keep .bay-controls outside the region that gets re-rendered.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Chromium with Playwright, using dist/preview.html with localStorage rex-lab-v1 = {action:'throw', angle:45}. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l04_drag.js, l04_drag2.js and l04_check.js.

**Cause**
- The angle slider is built inside the bay: bayThrow puts `.bay-controls` (object picker + angleControl) at parts[0].
- Its oninput (app.html:541) calls scheduleBay (app.html:1014). After 30 ms with no further input, that runs renderBay, and `bay.replaceChildren(...parts)` (app.html:1010) swaps in a brand-new `<input id=angle>`.
- Chromium ends a range-thumb drag when its element leaves the DOM. Moving the mouse after that does nothing.
- Restoring focus by id (app.html:1011) keeps arrow keys working, but it cannot bring back the drag.

**Results at 1280 px, mouse dragged from 45° toward about 9° in 30 steps**
- About 8 ms between moves: every input lands inside the debounce window, the timer never fires, and the drag reaches 7°.
- About 16 ms plus round-trip overhead: the value sticks at 41° from the 3rd step on and ends at "Launch angle: 41°".
- 50 ms between moves: it sticks at 44°.

findings.title: The Atlas feat's Simulate button shows a false failure: "It needs 1× more strength"
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:1142 runFeat (state.logKg = Math.log10(r.liftKg)), 430 ctx (Math.pow(10, logKg)), 677 bayLift verdict

Cause: Math.pow(10, Math.log10(5.1e18)) = 5.099999999999984e18, which is less than the sky mass of 5.1e18, so canLift=false with margin 0.9999999999999969. - ctx (app.html:430) rebuilds F = Math.pow(10, logKg)·g, which gives 5.099999999999984e18·g.

My script is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l06.js.

**Browser:** I used Playwright on dist/preview.html, which is current (built after the last change to src/app.html), and clicked Simulate on the Atlas card. The page shows:
- Dial: "Lifts 5.1 quadrillion t"
- Verdict: "Rex can’t budge it. It needs 1× more strength."
- Red chip: "Strength: 100% of what’s needed"
- Info chip: "Below: what would happen if he could"

Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l06_atlas.png. The feat sets Rex's strength equal to the load, so the correct result is that he lifts it (and sinks, because the ground fails). findings.evidence: Stomp at logKg 12, loaded at 844x390 (landscape), then rotated to 390x844: the blast chart keeps viewBox width 760 but renders at 324 px, so its 11 px text becomes 4.7 px (lay_rotate-stomp-390.png). verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Playwright with dist/preview.html, using my own script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l10.js and l10b.js.

Cause: the charts take their width from `chartW()` (app.html:548), which reads `#bay.clientWidth` only when the bay is rendered. The only resize listener (app.html:1179) calls `renderLadder` and never `renderBay`. The comment at app.html:547 says "Charts are drawn at the bay's real pixel width so text stays at its set size on phones". That promise breaks as soon as the width changes after load.

- **Phone rotated to portrait:** load at 844x390 and the bay is 778 px, the viewBox is 760 and text is 11.3 px. Rotate to 390x844 and the bay is 324 px but the viewBox stays 760, so 11 px text renders at **4.7 px**. The blast radii values ("742 m" and so on) and the axis labels can't be read. It stays that way until any setting changes.
- **Phone rotated to landscape:** load at 390x844 (viewBox 324), then rotate to 844x390. Text renders at **26.4 px** and the chart grows 2.4x. The trajectory chart becomes about 528 px tall.
- **Desktop window resize:** shrink the window from 1280 to 500 wide and the text drops to 6.3 px.
- **Address-bar changes:** a change in height alone does not change the result.

1. WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow) is not violated. There is no horizontal scroll at 320 px (overflow 0), and WCAG sets no minimum text size. This is a gap against the code's own design intent, not a WCAG failure.
2. The finding's fix for this (floor = `Math.min(300, bayWidth)`) makes the chart worse. `logBars` caps padL at w*0.5. The stomp blast label "Eardrums start to burst" already starts at x=-10 in the viewBox and is clipped at the 320 and 360 px viewports, and at x=-5 at 375 px (getBBox measured). At w=254, padL drops to 127, so the label would start near x=-33 and the bar area would shrink to about 43 px. That clipping is a separate small defect worth logging on its own.

Severity: I confirm minor, on the edge of major. The broken state is reachable and makes the chart unreadable, but it is transient and any interaction fixes it.

I tested the fix below on a patched copy (l10-fixed.html). After rotating to portrait the chart redraws with viewBox 324 and 11 px text. Rotating back gives 760 and 11.3 px. An open "Show the math" panel stays open, and a height-only resize does not trigger a re-render.

findings.title: The ladder's 18 marker buttons and all bar-chart values sit inside role="img" SVGs, which some screen readers drop
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:1056 (ladder svg role=img containing g role=button tabindex=0 at 1081), 610 logBars svg role=img aria-label=title only, 575 trajectoryChart
findings.evidence: ARIA 1.2 defines img with "Children Presentational: True". WebKit/VoiceOver and Firefox prune the subtree, so the 18 "Set strength here" buttons are focusable but unnamed and unreachable by screen-reader navigation. Chromium currently still exposes them (CDP AX tree shows 18 buttons). The blast-radius numbers (Windows shatter … Half of people killed) exist only inside an img labelled "Blast radius by damage level", and the jump landmarks, sprint references and pull forces are in the same position. Users of those screen readers never get the values.
findings.expected: Interactive markers exposed as buttons, and chart values available as text.
findings.fix: On the ladder, use role="group" with aria-label instead of img. For logBars, either put the values in the aria-label ("Windows shatter 293 km; Houses collapse 114 km; …") or add a visually hidden <table>/<ul> with the rows.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this, and the real reach is wider than the finding says, though one of its browser claims is wrong. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/ (l11.js, l11b.js, l11c.js).

1) The authoring error is confirmed. In src/app.html:1056 the ladder is `<svg role="img">` and it contains 18 `<g role="button" tabindex="0">` markers (line 1081). ARIA 1.2 gives img "Children Presentational: True". I injected axe-core 4.10.2 into dist/preview.html (logKg 9, stomp tab) and it reports `nested-interactive` (serious) on `svg[viewBox="0 0 900 804"]`: "Element has focusable descendants".

2) Browser behaviour, checked against engine source and live runs:
- **Chromium:** the CDP Blink tree does list the 18 buttons and the bar text, as the finding says. But that tree is not what screen readers get. Chromium's ui/accessibility/ax_node.cc `AXNode::IsLeaf()` returns true for kImage when the role attribute is "img". `BrowserAccessibility::PlatformChildCountWithoutAnnouncementNodes()` then returns 0 for leaves. So on Chrome and Edge, NVDA, JAWS, Narrator and VoiceOver see a childless image. The finding's "Chromium currently still exposes them" is wrong in the direction that makes the bug worse.
- **WebKit:** in current WebKit main, `AccessibilityObject::ariaRoleHasPresentationalChildren()` includes Image, and `defaultObjectInclusion()` ignores every descendant of such an element. Safari/VoiceOver therefore drops the buttons and the bar values, as claimed. I could not launch WebKit here (missing libgtk-4), so this rests on source alone.
- **Firefox:** this part of the finding is refuted. Firefox 1495 via Playwright shows all 18 "Set strength here" buttons and the bar-chart text leaves under the img nodes. Firefox's pruning only applies to a single text-leaf child.

3) The content loss is real. I removed every SVG and searched the remaining page text:
- **Blast radii:** "74.2 m, 25.2 m, 16.5 m, 8.1 m" appear nowhere else.
- **Ladder values:** all 18 marker values are missing. The 11 right-hand threshold markers (e.g. "Stomp = magnitude 7 quake, 40.9 quadrillion t") are not duplicated anywhere in text. The 7 left tier markers do have equivalents in the #tier-chips buttons.
- **Other charts:** the jump landmarks, sprint reference speeds and pull forces (except the resistance shown in the math line) exist only in the logBars SVG. That SVG's aria-label is just the title (line 610).
- **Trajectory chart:** a smaller loss. Range, apex and time are already in the tiles; only the no-air comparison curve is lost.

**Impact:** on Chromium and WebKit, which carry most screen-reader users, 18 focusable controls are effectively unnamed or unreachable, and four charts' data is unavailable. That fits "broken UI in a reachable state", so major stands. Sighted keyboard users are unaffected, and the headline verdicts and tiles remain readable, so it is not critical.

findings.title: The tab pattern is incomplete and verdict changes are never announced
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:242-243 (#tabs, #bay), 512-521 buttons and keydown, 191 aria-live on #dial-read
findings.evidence: The ARIA snapshot shows a tablist of 8 tabs and zero tabpanel nodes. #bay has no role=tabpanel or aria-labelledby, although every tab has aria-controls="bay". All 8 tabs are separate Tab stops (no roving tabindex), Home and End do nothing, and the tablist has no name. The only live region is #dial-read, so every slider step announces the dial text that the slider's aria-valuetext already gives, while the bay verdict ("The car flies 10 m…") is never announced.
findings.expected: WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, and the outcome of a change announced once.
findings.fix: Give #bay role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby set to the selected tab id. Set tabindex=-1 on unselected tabs and support Home/End. Give the tablist an aria-label of "Moves". Remove aria-live from #dial-read and add a visually hidden polite live region that receives the verdict text, debounced to about 500 ms.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced every part of this in Chromium with Playwright, using /home/user/dino-strength-sim/dist/preview.html and my script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l12.js. I could not refute any of it.

- **No tab panel.** The ARIA snapshot of `main "Test bay"` shows a tablist with 8 tabs. `getByRole('tabpanel')` returns 0. `#bay` has no role and no aria-labelledby, yet all 8 tabs set aria-controls="bay" (app.html:514 and 242-243).
- **Tablist has no name.** `#tabs` has neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby.
- **No roving tabindex.** Every tab has tabIndex 0. Pressing Tab from #tab-lift steps through tab-throw, jump, stomp, punch, clap, sprint and pull before it reaches obj, so the move tabs cost 8 Tab stops instead of 1.
- **Home and End do nothing.** With #tab-throw focused and selected, End and Home leave both focus and selection on tab-throw. ArrowRight works (moves to tab-jump). The keydown handler at app.html:516-520 only handles ArrowRight and ArrowLeft.
- **Only one live region, and it is the dial.** The only aria-live element on the page is `.dial-read` (app.html:191). `#bay` is not inside a live region and does not contain one.
  - One ArrowRight on the slider changed the dial from "Lifts 90.7 t / 890 kN…" to "Lifts 93.3 t / 915 kN… / ≈ 183× the strongest human". The slider's aria-valuetext was already "Lifts 93.3 t", so the first line is announced twice.
  - The bay's `p.verdict` ("The car flies 10 m. Rex gets shoved backward at 61.5 m/s.") is re-rendered on each change and is never announced.

One small overstatement: the dial region also says things the valuetext does not (force, the "× strongest human" comparison and preset names). So it is a partial duplicate, not a full one. The core claim holds: screen-reader users hear the dial on every step and never hear the outcome.

This is a real accessibility defect: an incomplete WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, and the main result of each interaction is not exposed. Under WCAG 4.1.3 the verdict is effectively a status message. It does not affect numbers or sighted users, so minor (comprehension and polish) is the right severity.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in Chromium using dist/preview.html with default settings, in both light and dark colour schemes (script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l13.js).

**Focus loss: confirmed.**

The accent box shows for keyboard focus only (`:focus-visible` is false after a mouse click), and it is clearly visible (l13-fixed-light.png).
verdict.better_fix:
Edit src/app.html in five places.

1. **Lines 1062 and 1064: give each marker a stable key.** The id `earth` appears in both the tier list and the threshold list, so the key needs a side prefix.
   - In `tierItems` add `key: 'L:' + t.id,` before `side: 'L'`.
   - In `thItems` add `key: 'R:' + t.id,` before `side: 'R'`.

2. **Line 1081: put the key on each marker group.**
```js
const g2 = sv('g', { class: 'mk', 'data-key': it.key, tabindex: '0', role: 'button', 'aria-label': ... });
```

3. **Line 1049: remember the focused marker before re-rendering.** Add this directly after `const wrap = $('#ladder-viz');`:
```js
const fk = wrap.contains(document.activeElement) ? document.activeElement.getAttribute('data-key') : null;
```

4. **Line 1104: restore focus after the SVG is replaced.** Add this directly after `wrap.replaceChildren(svg, tip);`. It mirrors what `renderBay` already does at lines 1009-1010:
```js
if (fk) { const n = svg.querySelector('[data-key="' + fk + '"]'); if (n) n.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }
```

5. **Line 1086 and the CSS: make focus visible on the label row.**
   - Give the existing hit-rect a class and rounded corners:
```js
g2.append(sv('rect', { class: 'hit', x: left ? 0 : axisX, y: it.ty - 14, width: axisX, height: 32, rx: 6, fill: 'transparent' }));
```
   - Add this CSS after line 139:
```css
.ladder-wrap svg .mk:focus-visible .hit { stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 2; }
```
   - Optionally, to also tint the row: move the rect so it is the first child of `g2`, which keeps the fill behind the text, and add `fill: var(--accent-wash);` to that rule.

findings.title: The ladder tooltip is clipped for the lowest markers
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:252 (.ladder-wrap also has class .viz with overflow-x:auto, so overflow-y computes to auto) and 1093 tooltip top
findings.evidence: Hovering or focusing Captain America at 390 puts the tooltip 98 px past the bottom of #ladder-viz, so it is cut off and only the title shows (lay_ladder-tip-clipped-390.png). Strongest human is 68 px past and Back-lift record 38 px. At 1280: 86, 48 and 10 px. The hidden part is the source and "who" note.
findings.expected: The full tooltip is visible.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this with Playwright on dist/preview.html, using default state and viewports of 390x900 and 1280x900, so I could not refute it. I fired pointerenter (and, separately, real hover and focus) on each ladder marker and measured the tooltip against #ladder-viz.

Why it happens: #ladder-viz has class "ladder-wrap viz". The rule `.viz { overflow-x: auto }` makes overflow-y compute to auto as well (getComputedStyle shows both as "auto"). The absolutely positioned .tip lives inside that box, and show() sets top = it.ty scaled + 22 px with no check against the bottom. For the lowest markers the tooltip runs past the box, scrollHeight grows beyond clientHeight, and the overflow is clipped into a scroll area.

How far the tooltip runs past the bottom of the box (my numbers match the finding exactly):

| Marker | 390 px | 1280 px |
|---|---|---|
| Captain America | 98 px (wrap 936, scrollHeight 1034) | 86 px |
| Strongest human | 68 px | 48 px |
| Back-lift record | 38 px | 10 px |
| "Jump clears the Statue of Liberty" threshold | 10 px | 1 px |

The finding did not mention the Statue of Liberty threshold. It sits low at default settings, and threshold positions move with mode, size and ground, so other thresholds can also land near the bottom.

Screenshots: scratchpad/audit2/l14/hover-cap-390.png and hover-cap-1280.png show only the black title band "Captain America" above the next section. The source note is hidden: "Official Handbook (1986): presses 800 lb ... heaviest log press on record (231 kg)". Keyboard focus gives the same 98 px overflow.

Severity: minor is right. Supplementary source/"who" text in a hover or focus tooltip is unreadable for the three lowest strength-level markers. No headline number is affected.

The finding's first suggested fix is wrong as written. Removing the .viz class would also drop the `.viz svg`, `.viz text` and `.viz .lbl-strong` rules that style the ladder's SVG and its labels (width, mono 11px font, fill colours). Horizontal scrolling is not needed here: the SVG is width:100% with a viewBox, so it scales down. Setting overflow back to visible is enough.

I checked the fix on a scratch copy (scratchpad/audit2/l14/preview-fixed.html with only that one CSS line changed). Computed overflow becomes visible, the whole tooltip shows at 320, 390 and 1280 (see fixed-cap-390.png), and there is no horizontal page overflow (document scrollWidth equals clientWidth at all three widths). The tooltip briefly overlaps the top of the "Famous feats" heading, which is normal for a tooltip (z-index 3).

findings.title: Results fade to about 47% opacity during a slider drag, and "Show the math" closes on every change
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:174 ('rise' animation on .verdict and .tiles), 1010 (bay.replaceChildren recreates the nodes on every input), 453 math()
findings.evidence: Opacity of .verdict sampled two frames after each step of a 30-step drag: 0.46-0.47 the whole time, because the 0.25 s animation from 0.4 restarts on every input event. That is an effective 3.3:1 in light mode, plus a 3 px jitter, while the user is watching the number change. Opening "Show the math" on Stomp and then moving the strength slider closes it again.
findings.expected: The result stays fully opaque while it updates, and the math panel stays open, so the equations can be watched as they change.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced both halves in Chromium using dist/preview.html with prefers-reduced-motion set to no-preference. My scripts are in scratchpad/audit2/l15.js, l15b.js and l15c.js.

Why it happens: the strength slider's input handler (app.html:500) calls update(), which calls renderBay() synchronously. renderBay() (line 1010) runs bay.replaceChildren(...), which creates a new .verdict, new .tiles and a new details.math every time. Line 174 attaches `animation: rise 0.25s` (opacity 0.4 to 1, translateY 3px) to every .verdict and .tiles, so each new node starts the fade again.

1) The fade. With action=lift, I dragged the slider 2 px every 16 ms (61 input events) and read the opacity of #bay .verdict once per animation frame. During the drag it alternated between 0.40 and 0.47: minimum 0.40, mean 0.44, maximum 0.59. After release it took about 13 frames to climb back to 1.00. The transform stayed at translateY of about 2.4 to 2.7 px for the whole drag. The verdict is 33.6 px weight-800 text, rgb(22,25,17), on the panel background rgb(246,247,241). Normally that is about 15:1 contrast. At opacity 0.40 to 0.47 it drops to about 2.6 to 3.2:1, so the finding's "about 3.3:1" is if anything generous. In short, the headline result is dimmed for as long as the user is moving the control that changes it.

Dragging the slider closed it again, and so did clicking the mode-real toggle. Any state change re-runs math(), which creates a new, closed details element. As a result, nobody can watch the equations change as they move the slider.
