No numbers are wrong and nothing is broken, but both effects get in the way of reading the result. Minor is the right severity.

findings.title: Settings changes block the main thread for 300-450 ms (1-1.5 s on a throttled CPU); slider moves are fast
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:1019-1045 thresholds() runs every P.threshold bisection synchronously in one setTimeout task; the cache keeps only one key
findings.evidence: Slider re-render in real-muscle mode, layout included, is at most 19 ms on every tab (worst: Jump), and at most 66 ms at 4× CPU throttle, so slider moves are fine. Settings changes are not. Real-muscle Size → Kaiju: ladder appears after 433 ms, with the main thread blocked (1,554 ms at 4×). Real → Comic: 329 ms (975 ms at 4×). Surface or ground toggle: 150-275 ms. Culprits, timed in Node (thprof.js). Comic at 2 m: Stomp quake3 136 ms, jumpliberty 98 ms, carmach3 46 ms. Real at 50 m: jumpliberty 223 ms, jumpRigid 143 ms. Each runs 22 bisection steps of P.jump or P.stomp.
findings.expected: No main-thread task over about 300 ms after an input.
findings.fix: Cache thresholds in a Map keyed by settings, so toggling back is instant. Compute one threshold per setTimeout or requestIdleCallback chunk and draw the ladder progressively. Cut the bisection to about 15 steps (0.001-decade precision is plenty for 3 significant figures).

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this with my own scripts in scratchpad/audit2/l16/ (node_th.js, pw.js, pw2.js). The finding is real and minor is the right severity.

**Code path.** Every control (mode, size chips, height, mass, surface, ground-holds, anchor) calls `update()`. That calls `renderBay()` straight away, then `scheduleLadder()`, which runs `renderLadder()` after 120 ms. `renderLadder` calls `thresholds()` (app.html:1019-1045). That function runs 10 or 11 `P.threshold` bisections back to back (engine.js:819; tolerance 1e-4, about 22 predicate calls each) in a single task. Its cache holds only one key (`thCache = {key, list}`).

**Node timing of the exact `thresholds()` body:**
- Comic, 2 m: 267 ms total (quake3 140, jumpliberty 98, carmach3 28).
- Real, 50 m: 387 ms (jumpliberty 299, boom 43).
- Comic, 50 m: 422 ms (quake3 197, jumpliberty 143, carmach3 79).
- Real, 2 m: 36 ms, because most thresholds there are unreachable and return after 2 calls.
- A CPU profile shows the time goes to `fly()`, `rhoAt()` and `acc()`: flight integration inside `P.stomp` and `P.jump`.

**Browser test (Playwright on dist/preview.html, PerformanceObserver 'longtask'), at 1x CPU:**

| Click | Long task | Ladder redrawn |
|---|---|---|
| Real → Kaiju | 299-300 ms | +461 ms |
| Kaiju → Comic | 366-391 ms | +507-552 ms |
| Back to 2 m | 171-204 ms | |
| Ground-holds toggle | 172-221 ms | |
| Comic again | 183-215 ms | |

At 4x throttle the same clicks give 630-1260 ms tasks; Kaiju takes 1019-1258 ms to redraw. Slider sweeps give no long tasks at 1x and one of 77 ms at 4x. So the headline claim holds.

**Corrections to the evidence:**
1. The "jumpRigid 143 ms at real 50 m" figure comes from their script running jumpRigid unconditionally. The page computes `withRigid` only when jumpliberty is unreachable, and at real 50 m it is reachable.
2. The click's own response is not blocked. `renderBay` runs synchronously and paints before the 120 ms-delayed ladder task, so bay text and chip state update at once. The freeze hits only the ladder update and any tap or scroll made in the next 0.2-0.4 s (about 1 s on a slow phone).

No number or claim is wrong, and nothing is broken, so this is minor, not major.

**On their proposed fix:**
- A Map cache only helps when toggling back to a setting already computed.
- One threshold per task still leaves a single 300 ms task (real 50 m jumpliberty), or about 1.2 s at 4x.
- Cutting to 15 steps saves only about 25% and makes labels up to 0.23% high.

**Side note, out of scope:** a separate 350-550 ms block at page load comes from `calibrateComic()` running when engine.js loads (447-553 ms in Node). The fix below does not touch it.

**Fix tested.** I applied the fix below to a scratch copy, preview_patched.html:
- At 1x there are no long tasks on any settings change.
- At 4x the worst is 199 ms, and that is the synchronous `renderBay`, not the ladder.
- Ladder redraw time is unchanged or better: Kaiju +478 ms, Comic +374 ms, toggles back +143-152 ms from cache.
- The ladder output, read from all marker aria-labels, is identical to the original in all 20 states, including rapid Real→Kaiju→Comic clicking.
- No console errors.

findings.title: First screen and ADHD clarity: on phones no result is visible, the bay opens with controls rather than its verdict, the ladder has no verdict line, and "Pick a feat" points the wrong way
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:178-186 hero, 184 .start steps, 671-682 and 711-738 (object/angle picker pushed before the verdict), 247-254 ladder section
findings.evidence: At 390x844 the hero fills the top half of the screen and the dial the rest (lay_fold-390-light.png). The tabs start at y=928 and the first verdict at y=1206, so moving the slider visibly changes only the dial number. In Lift, Throw and Pull the bay opens with the object select and angle slider, and the verdict comes after them. The ladder section (about 920 px tall on a phone, 18 markers) has no one-line summary of where Rex is. Step 2 says "Pick a feat", but the control is a row of moves (Lift…Pull); "Famous feats" is a different section further down. At 1280 the verdict is visible at y=480, which is fine.
findings.expected: Each panel leads with its one-line result, and the first screen shows the effect of step 1.
findings.fix: Below 920 px, shrink the hero (72 px image, one-sentence lede) and add a one-line live verdict under the slider. Render the verdict before .bay-controls. Add a ladder summary line, e.g. "At 90.7 t Rex is past: fist breaks the sound barrier, jump clears the Statue of Liberty. Next: clap breaks windows at 2,500 t." Rename step 2 to "Pick a move".

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced the measurements with Playwright on dist/preview.html. The scripts are l17.js and l17b.js in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/. The positions are correct, but none of the parts is a defect. Each one is a design preference or a feature request.

At 390x844 the hero runs from y=20 to 429 and the slider sits at y=601. The tabs are at 928. The first verdict is at y=1123 for Lift and Pull and y=1206 for Throw. So on the first screen at load, no physics verdict is visible.

1) "The first screen shows no effect of step 1" is not true. The dial readout on that first screen is step 1's result, and it updates as the slider moves. At the default state it reads "Lifts 90.7 t", "890 kN of force (504x his body weight)" and "Hulk & Thor (Class 100) ... in excess of 100 tons", and the active preset chip changes too (fold-390.png). "Changes only the dial number" overstates it. The hero itself lists the order: set strength, then pick a move, then read what breaks. The phone layout stacks things in that same order.

2) The "turn the dial and watch the physics" loop works on phones after one scroll. The distance from the top of the slider to the bottom of the verdict is 548 to 657 px on 375x667, 390x844 and 412x915. That fits inside every one of those viewports. covis-390-throw.png is a screenshot after scrolling to y=590: the slider, presets, tabs, object select, angle slider, the verdict "The car flies 10 m. Rex gets shoved backward at 61.5 m/s." and the status chips all fit on one screen.

3) "The verdict comes after the object/angle controls" describes inputs placed before the output they set, which is the normal order. The controls are 65 px tall in Lift and Pull and 148 px in Throw. The verdict is still about 80 to 280 px below the tab row. That is a layout choice, not broken UI.

4) "The ladder has no verdict line" is a feature request. The ladder draws a labelled "now" line across all 18 markers (renderLadder, app.html:1073-1074). Every marker also has a tooltip and is clickable. Nothing on the ladder is wrong or mislabelled.

5) "Pick a feat points the wrong way" does not hold. Lift, Throw and Jump are feats of strength in the ordinary sense. Reading top to bottom, the first thing a phone user can pick after step 1 is the tab row, directly below the controls panel. The "Famous feats" section is more than 1,000 px further down, past the ladder. Even a user who does go there finds a "Simulate" button on each card. That button (runFeat) sets the move, scrolls back to the rig and shows the result. So that path leads to the same outcome rather than a dead end.

No number is wrong, no claim is false and nothing is broken. The suggested fixes (smaller hero, a sticky live verdict, reordering, a summary line) are UX redesign wishes. The audit brief says to skip style preferences.
verdict.better_fix: No fix is needed. One optional wording change: the ladder intro calls the tabs "an everyday move", so step 2 could match it. In app.html line 184, change `2 Pick a feat` to `2 Pick a move`.

findings.title: The Stomp "He gets launched" tile repeats the same text at relativistic speed
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:869
findings.evidence: Stomp at logKg 20 (390 or 1280) shows the tile "He gets launched / 93.9% of light speed / 93.9% of light speed" (lay_stomp-390-krakatoa.png), because speedOnly() returns the same string as fmtSpeed() when the speed is above 1% of c.
findings.expected: No duplicated line.
findings.fix: Set the sub-line to '' when bf.relativistic, or to the Lorentz factor.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in headless Chromium against dist/preview.html. I set localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' = {logKg, inf:false, action:'stomp'} and read the "He gets launched" tile. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l18.js and l18b.js.

What the page shows:
- logKg 20 at 1280 and 390 width: ["He gets launched","93.9% of light speed","93.9% of light speed"]
- logKg 17: "2.34% of light speed" twice
- logKg 19: "39.3% of light speed" twice
- logKg 21: "99.910486% of light speed" twice
- logKg 26 and up, and Infinite: "light speed (to the last digit)" twice

Cause: app.html:869 uses fmtSpeed(r.vBody) for the value when bf.relativistic, and speedOnly(r.vBody) for the sub-line. speedOnly (line 668) is fmtSpeed(v).split(' · ')[0]. The engine sets relativistic at v0 > 0.01c (engine.js:379), and fmtSpeed switches to the bare "% of light speed" string at v >= 0.01c. So in every relativistic stomp state the two strings are identical. That covers all reachable strengths from about logKg 17 up to the slider maximum of 34, plus Infinite.

Below that threshold the tile is fine. For example, logKg 16 shows "9.47 km up / 2,190,000 m/s". This is a comprehension and polish defect, not a wrong number, so minor is the right severity.

Related, more serious bug found during the sweep (same formatter, a separate finding): at logKg 24 and 25 the tile and the verdict read "1% of light speed", but the true speed is about 99.9999999+% of c. In fmtSpeed, sig(b*100, 8) rounds to 100, toLocaleString gives "100", and .replace(/0+$/, '') strips it to "1". The replace is otherwise a no-op, because toLocaleString already drops trailing fractional zeros. This affects every caller of fmtSpeed in that band, including the sprint top speed and the stomp verdict. It is a wrong headline number in a reachable state (major) and should be logged on its own.
verdict.better_fix:
In app.html:869, drop the sub-line when the main value already shows the speed:

  tile('He gets launched', r.vBody > 0.5 ? (bf.relativistic ? fmtSpeed(r.vBody) : (bf.escaped ? 'Escapes Earth' : fmtDist(bf.apex) + ' up')) : 'no', r.vBody > 0.5 && !bf.relativistic ? speedOnly(r.vBody) : '')

Optionally, use the Lorentz factor as the relativistic sub-line, e.g. bf.relativistic && isFinite(r.vBody) ? 'Lorentz factor ' + sig(1/Math.sqrt(1-(r.vBody/K.c)**2), 3) : ...

Related fix for the separate "1% of light speed" bug in fmtSpeed (app.html ~382). Replace
  if (b > 0.999) return sig(b * 100, 8).replace(/0+$/, '') + '% of light speed';
with
  if (b > 0.999) { const s = sig(b * 100, 8); return (s === '100' ? 'over 99.999999' : s) + '% of light speed'; }

findings.title: Saved settings are not validated: stale or corrupt storage breaks the bay. Blocked storage is handled correctly.
findings.location: /home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/app.html:416-420 (Object.assign(state, saved); only surface and obj are checked)
findings.evidence: With localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' set to {"action":"fly"}, the bay shows "Calculation failed: BAYS[state.action] is not a function" with no tab selected, until the user clicks a tab. {"mode":"cartoon"} leaves neither Comic nor Real pressed while the summary says "Comic book". {"anchor":"glued"} makes the summary read "Comic book · Concrete slab ·  · 2 m". {"H":1e6} bypasses the 500 m cap, and {"logKg":null} gives "Lifts 1 kg", below the slider minimum. With storage blocked (a localStorage getter that throws SecurityError) or setItem throwing QuotaExceeded, the page works normally.
findings.expected: Unknown or out-of-range saved values fall back to their defaults.
findings.fix: After loading, validate each key: action in ACTIONS, mode in {comic, real}, anchor in {friction, braced, bolted}, H in [0.1, 500], m > 0, logKg a finite number in [1, 34], angle in [0, 90], inf boolean. Otherwise use the DEFAULTS value.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced every case in Chromium against file:///home/user/dino-strength-sim/dist/preview.html. My script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/audit2/l19.js. It writes 'rex-lab-v1' and then reloads the page.
- {"action":"fly"}: the bay shows "Calculation failed: BAYS[state.action] is not a function", no tab is selected, and the console logs a TypeError.
- {"mode":"cartoon"}: Comic and Real are both aria-pressed=false, but the summary says "Comic book".
- {"anchor":"glued"}: the select is blank and the summary reads "Comic book · Concrete slab ·  · 2 m".
- {"H":1000000}: the summary shows "1,000,000 m" even though the UI caps height at 500 m.
- {"logKg":null}: the dial shows "Lifts 1 kg" (Math.pow(10, null) = 1), below the slider minimum of 10 kg.
- {"m":null}: the dial shows "(∞× his body weight)" and the mass box shows 0.

The cause is src/app.html:416-420. Object.assign(state, saved) copies every saved key, and only surface and obj are checked afterwards. dist/index.html:4304 has the same code. Blocked or throwing storage is handled correctly by the try/catch blocks.

What limits this to minor: the page itself never writes these values. Every control clamps or limits its own input:
- the strength slider is limited to 1..34;
- height is clamped to 0.1..500;
- mass accepts only m > 0;
- the angle slider is limited to 0..90;
- action, mode and anchor come only from fixed buttons and options.

I checked the strength values the page can set. All tiers (2.56..24.78) and feat presets (log10 up to 24.78, plus Infinity through inf=true) fall inside [1, 34]. I also tried to inject an invalid mass through the UI by typing 1e400. Chromium's number input rejects it, so nothing changed. The key is new ('-v1') and no older schema exists anywhere in the repo or tests.

So no current visitor can hit this through normal use. It happens only with hand-edited storage, an extension or another page writing the same key (Chromium gives all file:// pages one shared localStorage), or a future release that renames an action, mode or anchor id without bumping the key. Clicking a tab, mode button or control repairs the state.

It is still a real gap. Half the keys are validated and half are not, and the failure shows an internal JS error message to users. Severity stays minor and the priority is low: it is hardening, not a factual error.
